| F.73 | —     | A successful PDF render logs nothing, so 'did it render?' cannot be answered from logs                                                  | ⏳     | —          | Found on 2026-09-14 while trying to confirm the first production render after the Typst cutover. A gap in observability, not in the renderer. THE FAULT, verified in code: apps/workers/src/jobs/render-pdf.ts contains ZERO logger calls — neither runRenderPdf nor handleRenderPdfJob logs anything on success — and nothing else on the path does either: the same grep over apps/workers/src/pdf/, apps/web/lib/pdf/render-request.ts and apps/web/lib/actions/quotations/generate-pdf.ts is empty. So a completed render is indistinguishable from one that never happened. THE FIX IS ALREADY HALF-BUILT, which is the part worth knowing: `pdf.generated` is ALREADY DECLARED in the trackEvent contract on both sides — apps/workers/src/observability/event-types.ts:52 and apps/web/lib/observability/event-types.ts:52, typed as { documentId: string; documentType: string } — and it is EMITTED NOWHERE. The only reference in application code outside the two declarations is a web test (apps/web/lib/observability/events.test.ts:67); the name also appears in BUILD_PROMPTS.md:4916, in the Day 17 contract that declared it. This is the placeholder pattern: a declared value with nothing writing it is not an implementation. So the work is to emit an event the contract already reserves, matching how email/handler.ts:143 emits `email.sent`, rather than to design new telemetry — and trackEvent ships to Axiom, so the record outlives DO's run-log buffer. BUT NOT TO THE RUN LOG, which is the thing this task is about: both sinks are EITHER/OR, not both — apps/workers/src/observability/events.ts:62-70 and apps/web/lib/observability/events.ts:114-124 return immediately after the Axiom ingest when NODE_ENV=production and a client and dataset are configured, so the logger.info at workers :72 / web :128 is unreachable in production and the only pino calls left inside trackEvent are its two failure warns (workers :65 and :68, web :118 and :122). So emitting pdf.generated gives durable evidence in Axiom and STILL leaves the DO run log silent. If run-log visibility is wanted too — and the whole reason this task exists is that the run log could not answer "did it render?" — the wiring needs an explicit logger call ALONGSIDE trackEvent, not instead of it. Decide that deliberately. Consider widening the payload to carry generatedDocumentId, sizeBytes and duration_ms; keep tenant data to ids only, per docs/LOGGING.md's eight-stream surface. pdf-cleanup IS ALREADY INSTRUMENTED and is the model to copy, not a second gap — jobs/pdf-cleanup.ts:42 logs 'pdf-cleanup sweep complete' with its result, and jobs/validity-expiry.ts:65 does the same; the first version of this task wrongly listed pdf-cleanup as also missing telemetry, and someone acting on that would have 'fixed' a job that was already correct. PRECISION ABOUT WHICH SURFACE REPORTS WHAT, because it is the whole question: apps/workers/src/index.ts makes exactly TWO logger calls, :71 on start and :94 on start failure. captureJobError in observability/sentry.ts is Sentry.captureException and does NOT reach the log stream at all. The third failure log is queue/boss.ts:68 ('pg-boss error'), not in index.ts. WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW than under Chromium: the old path had a warm-up line, recycle logs with reasons, and a cold-start signature, so render activity was visible as a side effect of the browser's lifecycle. Typst has no lifecycle, so that incidental visibility went with the browser. COMPOUNDING FACTOR, observed twice in six hours: DO App Platform's run-log buffer is short and a deploy rotates it. PR #24 (docs only) redeployed both apps at 09:51 UTC, and PR #25 redeployed them again at ~16:04 (NOT docs-only, unlike #24: it added scripts/check-id-references.mjs and its allowlist, and touched package.json, the verify workflow and two seed files) — each time discarding the window containing the render under investigation. SHARPER, AND WORSE, established 2026-09-14 while trying to confirm a second production render: the run log cannot distinguish a SUCCESSFUL render from a FAILED one. Success logs nothing, as recorded above — but failure does not reach the run log either. instrumentJobHandler (observability/sentry.ts:60-78) captures a throwing job to Sentry via captureJobError (sentry.ts:40-47) and rethrows; pg-boss then RETRIES IT TWICE WITH NO BACKOFF — three attempts in total. The exact figure matters for anyone verifying a render by counting Sentry events: retryLimit=5 with retryBackoff is EMAIL_QUEUE_RETRY (queue/boss.ts:19-22), applied at boss.ts:72-73 only when queue === EMAIL_QUEUE. RENDER_PDF_QUEUE is created bare at boss.ts:75 and takes pg-boss 10.4.2's default retry_limit of 2. So expect three captures in rapid succession, not five spread out. The only pg-boss logging is instance.on('error') at queue/boss.ts:67-69, which is an INSTANCE-level handler for pg-boss's own failures, not a per-job one. So a render that throws — for example because the Typst binary is missing in the image — produces an ACTIVE, healthy-looking workers process and a silent run log, and is visible only in Sentry and in the absence of a generated_documents row. That is why the first two attempts to confirm a production render from logs could not succeed in either direction, and it is the strongest argument for emitting the already-declared pdf.generated event: it converts 'no evidence' into 'positive evidence', which is a different thing. When wiring it, emit on the failure path too, or the log still answers only half the question. STALE COMMENT TO FIX WHILE DOING THIS WORK, recorded here rather than on F.74 because F.74 is an enumeration task that touches no code: apps/workers/src/index.ts:10-11 still describes the render-pdf web path as spawning a one-shot CLI per DEV.36, but render-request.ts:69 enqueues through pg-boss per DEV.63 — the comment has been wrong since Stage C. Note the emit itself lands in jobs/render-pdf.ts, not index.ts, so this is an adjacent fix rather than an incidental one; do it deliberately or it will be missed. |

| F.3   | 35    | Multi-rate tax summary — data layer + screens                                                                                                                   | ✅     | 2026-09-20 | BLOCKED ON F.81 AND F.55 — recorded here as well as on those tasks so the constraint is visible from whichever task is picked up first, the same reason F.4 and F.6 each carry their shared sequencing note. (1) F.81 (multi-rate seed data + mixed-rate reference case) MUST LAND FIRST. This task builds a multi-rate GST summary against a corpus that contains no multi-rate document: `packages/db/src/seeds/day5.ts:259-337` generates 20 products, every one at `gstRate: '18'` and `hsnCode: '85414300'`, and none of the 14 cases in `apps/workers/scripts/typst-matrix.json` is mixed-rate. Every assertion written here before F.81 would be written against a single-rate fixture and would pass whether or not the feature works. Per CLAUDE.md §11.1 ruling 4, the fix is deterministic seed data, not an excluded assertion. (2) F.55 (the 3% rate-list mismatch) SHOULD BE RESOLVED FIRST, because this task groups and keys by rate and F.55 records that nine separate rate-list constants omit 3 while the DB CHECK accepts it — measured 2026-09-17, `computeTax` throws `INVALID_GST_RATE` on a 3% line. Until F.55 is resolved, 5% and 18% are the safe rates to build and seed against; 3% is not. (3) WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND FOR THIS TASK, in full: `docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md` (merged, PR #36), especially §1 (every render site and whether it assumes one rate), §2 (no rate-keyed or HSN-keyed aggregation exists anywhere — established against the closed set of all 22 GROUP BY keys) and §3 (every `gstRate` read and whether it normalises). Two results bear directly on the data layer this task builds: the on-screen surface is `apps/web/app/(app)/quotations/_components/summary-card.tsx:37-45`, which today renders the literal word `mixed` when rates differ, and its data source `apps/web/lib/quotation/preview.ts:52-61` returns `{cgst, sgst, igst}` as three scalars, so there is no rate-group array for a screen to render even if one wanted to. The engine's own output has the same shape — `TaxComputationOutput` (packages/tax/src/types.ts:58-77) carries seven flat scalars plus a POSITIONAL `lines[]` keyed by `lineId`, with `gstRate` as a per-line payload field and no `hsnCode` at all. MEASURED AND SETTLED, so it need not be re-derived: the `'18'` vs `'18.00'` hazard CLAUDE.md §5 warns about CANNOT arise from a read of the four rate columns — they are `decimal(5,2)`, so Postgres returns the canonical `'18.00'` for every input spelling and the two collapse to a single `Set` member (verified 2026-09-17 on Postgres 16.15 through postgres.js 3.4.9 + drizzle-orm 0.45.2; see docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md §8.1 and DEV.135). The three existing `Set`-by-rate sites all normalise already. The hazard that IS live is a DB string compared against a non-DB string, which is a different mechanism from the one §5 describes. BUILT 2026-09-20, PR pending. Ran from docs/F3_DAY_PROMPT.md, APPROVED, D-1 to D-8 settled; two of the drafter's recommendations had been overruled by the operator (D-4, D-7) and one required amending the spec (D-2). THE COMPUTATION: packages/tax/src/summary.ts, new and additive — computeTaxSummary returns byRate plus byHsn plus document totals, computeRateSummary returns the rate half for callers with no HSN. computeTax itself is unchanged, no existing export changed behaviour, no fixture touched; compute.test.ts still reports its original 54 cases. TWO ERRORS IN THE SPEC, BOTH MINE, BOTH FOUND BY BUILDING RATHER THAN READING. First, section 3's money rule named per-line tax columns that do not exist at any grain — corrected in place, dated, and the replacement derives through computeTax over the stored lines, which templates/quotation.tsx:186-196 already does on every PDF render. Second, section 2's HSN table said one row per HSN with a scalar rate, which is incoherent when one HSN carries two rates — the case Chain B seeds deliberately. The operator rejected a nullable rate because a null rate cannot resolve a Tally ledger, which is what F.11 needs the table for, so the key is the (HSN, rate) PAIR and Chain B correctly yields three HSN rows. THE PAISA THAT IS NOT F.3'S: computeTax derives discountAmount at document level but allocates it per line with per-line rounding, so on a discounted document sum(lineDiscount) can exceed discountAmount by 0.01 and sum(lineTaxable) fall short of taxableAmount by the same 0.01. Filed as F.101, sequenced before F.4. F.3 asserts the identities exactly on undiscounted documents and CHARACTERISES the delta on discounted ones, in a test whose own comment says it asserts a figure wrong by one paisa on purpose and must fail when F.101 lands. THE SCREENS: one shared component, apps/web/components/tax/tax-summary-block.tsx, at all four sites — the builder via preview.byRate, and the three saved views via one adapter, apps/web/lib/tax/document-summary.ts. The literal 'mixed' label is gone. P-7 closes because every row now names its rate; P-8 closes via a minDecimals option on formatINRExact plus a named formatTaxAmount wrapper, chosen over changing groupedINR's default because that is 121 call sites across 30 files. THE EVIDENCE THAT THE DEFAULT IS UNCHANGED IS THAT ALL 30 PRE-EXISTING FORMAT TESTS PASS UNTOUCHED, not that the diff looks safe. THE REPORT: gst-summary gains a groupBy param with arms state (default), rate and hsn, landed at all three R-9 sites — resolve.ts's arm, the page's own call, and the DownloadCsv params — plus the filter field. The rate and HSN arms carry NO tax amounts, which is the report's no-tax-package contract and not an omission; F.11 consumes F.3's computation instead. Their money column is named "Line value (pre-discount)" because sum(order_lines.line_total) is pre-discount and a post-discount per-rate figure would need the engine; 2 of 44 seeded orders carry a discount so the two coincide on 42, which is exactly why the label must say so. The Orders total is NULL on the bucketed axes because an order appears under every rate it carries and summing the buckets would overstate it. | F.105 | —     | AUDIT ONLY — BEFORE F.101: does the production order path derive place_of_supply from the tenant's state instead of the ship-to's?                              | ✅     | 2026-09-23 | Filed 2026-09-23 by operator ruling, split out of F.103 so that its POSITION carries the sequencing rather than a sentence in a notes field. THE REASONING FOR THE SPLIT, in the operator's terms: prose in a notes field is not enforcement, array position is. F.103 said "diagnose before F.4" and nothing made that true; this row sits before F.101 in the array, which is where a reader looking for what comes next will actually see it. THIS IS AUDIT ONLY. Read code, report a verdict, change nothing. No fix, no migration, no reseed, no test. The deliverable is a written answer to one question and the evidence for it. THE QUESTION: does the PRODUCTION order-creation path set orders.place_of_supply from the TENANT's state rather than from the SHIP-TO dealer's state? THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROMPTED IT, from F.103: 34 of 68 seeded orders have place_of_supply different from their ship_to_dealer.state — exactly half — and ORD-2026-0003 stores place_of_supply MH against a ship-to dealer in AS. Under ADR-012 and CLAUDE.md section 5 the ship-to state IS the place of supply for goods per IGST Act 2017 section 10, so a document like that reads intra-state and would be taxed CGST plus SGST when it should be IGST. HOW TO ANSWER IT — BY READING THE WRITE PATH, NOT BY COUNTING MORE ROWS: enumerate every site that writes orders.place_of_supply and report, for each, what it reads. status-transitions.ts builds order lines on PI confirmation and is the first place to look; the seeds are day12.ts and day13.ts. Do the same for quotations.place_of_supply and performa_invoices.place_of_supply, because the same derivation may be shared or may differ per document type — and a quotation legitimately has no separate ship-to, which CLAUDE.md section 5 already records, so the quotation answer is expected to differ and that is not a defect. TWO OUTCOMES, AND THEY DIFFER IN SEVERITY. If the PRODUCTION path is correct and only the seed is wrong, this is fixture corruption: bounded, but the 14 reference PDFs are captured from seeded documents so they ENCODE the wrong tax type, and correcting the seed would move reference renders and need a deliberate re-baseline. If the PRODUCTION path derives from tenant state, it is a live tax-classification defect on real documents and it may OUTRANK F.101 — which is precisely why this audit runs first: better known before investing a protected-surface engine day than after. WHY THIS IS NOT FOLDED INTO F.101's DAY: that day edits computeTax under a bounded authorisation and should not carry an unrelated tax-correctness investigation alongside it. Operator instruction. WHY IT IS CHEAP: read-only, no database mutation, no build, no reseed — it is a code read plus a written verdict, which is why it can sit in front of a bigger day without costing much. ON REPORTING: name the instrument behind any negative-existence claim and prefer affirmative enumeration over a clean search (CLAUDE.md section 11.1 rulings 7 and 8) — "here is the complete list of writers and what each reads" is evidence; "no hits for tenant_state" is not. Do NOT fix anything found. Report, and let the operator choose. Cross-references F.103, which holds the measurement and the decision, and F.5a, which also concerns place of supply. REFINEMENT 2026-09-23, OPERATOR — THE METHOD AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. This row said to enumerate every site that writes orders.place_of_supply and report what each reads. That is not enough, and the reason is the thing that makes the 34/68 split hard to read in the first place. SEPARATE THE WRITE SITES FROM THE DERIVATION OF THE VALUE WRITTEN. A seed module that calls a shared helper which derives place_of_supply wrongly is A PRODUCTION DEFECT WEARING SEED CLOTHES: the wrong value reaches the database through a seed file, so a writer-only enumeration files it under "seed", while the faulty logic is shared code that the production path may use too. The converse is also possible and equally misleading — a production action that inlines a correct derivation beside a seed that inlines a wrong one looks like one defect and is two independent ones. SO REPORT BOTH, AS TWO LISTS: first every WRITE SITE for the column, and second every DERIVATION — every distinct expression or helper that computes the value, whether inline at the write site or in shared code. THEN, FOR EACH WRITE SITE, SAY WHICH DERIVATION IT USES. That mapping is the deliverable; either list alone cannot distinguish the two cases this audit exists to tell apart. SECOND REFINEMENT — THE QUESTION MAY NOT BE ABOUT ORDERS ALONE. Report whether place_of_supply is stored on quotations and performa_invoices as well, and if it is, run the same write-site-and-derivation analysis for each. IF THE DERIVATION IS SHARED, A DEFECT IN IT REACHES THREE DOCUMENT TYPES RATHER THAN ONE, and F.4 prints the tax type — CGST plus SGST against IGST — on all three. That changes the blast radius from one table to the whole document chain, and it changes what a fix has to touch. KEEP THE EXPECTED DIFFERENCE IN MIND WITHOUT LETTING IT HIDE A REAL ONE: a quotation legitimately has no separate ship-to, so CLAUDE.md section 5 records that its place_of_supply is the dealer's own state — that is correct behaviour and not a finding. What WOULD be a finding is a PI or an order sharing the quotation's derivation, because those do carry a distinct ship-to and ADR-012 makes the ship-to state the place of supply for goods. STILL AUDIT ONLY: report the two lists, the mapping, and the three-document-type answer. Fix nothing. COMPLETED 2026-09-23. VERDICT: NO — the production order path does not derive place_of_supply from the tenant's state, on any of the three document types. The full report, with all database measurements, is docs/F105_AUDIT.md. THE ANSWER IN ONE CHAIN: orders.place_of_supply has exactly one production write site, status-transitions.ts:153, and it COPIES the PI's value; the PI's own derivation is (input.placeOfSupplyOverride ?? shipTo.state).toUpperCase() at convert-quotation-to-pi.ts:71 and update-pi.ts:41, which is ADR-012-correct. STRONGER THAN CURRENTLY CORRECT: dealers.state is nullable (schema/dealer.ts:54) so a tenant-state fallback was AVAILABLE, and loadDealerForDocument at pi/helpers.ts:152-154 throws VALIDATION rather than taking it — the production path refuses to produce the bad value instead of substituting one. The only ?? tenantState fallbacks in the repository are in two seed derivations. THE THREE DOCUMENT TYPES DO NOT SHARE A DERIVATION: seven distinct expressions write the column and no PI or order write site uses a quotation-shaped one, so the blast radius is DATA, not LOGIC, and a fix is scoped to two seed files. The quotation difference (its place_of_supply is its own dealer's state) is expected per CLAUDE.md section 5 and is not a finding. WHAT THE AUDIT ADDED BEYOND THE QUESTION: the 38-versus-34 arithmetic is now MEASURED rather than inferred — 19 hardcoded orders per tenant, 2 coincidentally agreeing, 17 mismatching, times 2 tenants; a SECOND symptom on the same inserts, tenant_state_at_issue also hardcoded 'MH' against the sample tenant's actual KA, folded into F.103 by operator ruling; and the finding that THE 14 REFERENCE PDFS ARE NOT AFFECTED, so F.103 needs no re-baseline and is cheaper than its filing assumed. Also recorded: no test asserts either invariant, and there is no test module for the PI or order server actions at all. METHOD: two independent passes agreeing — code-auditor for the writer and derivation enumerations by affirmative enumeration over a complete 94-file population, the main thread for the write-path read and every database measurement. Nothing was fixed; F.103 holds the fix. | F.103 | —     | HIGH — FIX THE SEED: day12 and day13 hardcode 'MH' for BOTH place_of_supply and tenant_state_at_issue, so 38 orders and 38 PIs store a wrong tax classification | ✅     | 2026-09-23 | Found 2026-09-22 while pinning verify-day-16's accessibility scan to an intra-state order during F.3's a11y fix. NOT DIAGNOSED — deliberately, because it was found on an unrelated branch and diagnosing it there would have folded a tax-correctness investigation into an accessibility fix. THE MEASUREMENT: of 68 seeded orders carrying a ship_to_dealer_id, 34 have place_of_supply equal to the ship-to dealer's state and 34 do NOT. Exactly half. THE CONCRETE CASE: ORD-2026-0003 in the demo tenant stores tenant_state_at_issue = MH and place_of_supply = MH, while its ship-to dealer Patel Renewables is in AS. Its bill-to dealer is also in AS. So place_of_supply equals the TENANT's state rather than the ship-to state. WHY THIS MIGHT BE A CORRECTNESS DEFECT AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING: ADR-012 and CLAUDE.md section 5 make PLACE OF SUPPLY THE SHIP-TO LOCATION for goods, per IGST Act 2017 section 10. Under that rule ORD-2026-0003 is an INTER-STATE supply and must carry IGST. As stored it reads intra-state, which would classify it as CGST plus SGST. That is a wrong tax type on a document, not a cosmetic disagreement. THE ROW MUST SEPARATE TWO CASES BECAUSE THEY DIFFER IN SEVERITY. CASE A, A SEED DEFECT: the seed code sets place_of_supply from the tenant or the bill-to rather than the ship-to. Bad but bounded — it corrupts fixture data, and because the 14 reference PDFs are captured from seeded documents THE REFERENCES THEN ENCODE THE WRONG TAX TYPE, so a corrected seed would move reference renders and require deliberate re-baselining. CASE B, A LIVE BUG: the production order-creation path derives place_of_supply from tenant state rather than ship-to state. That is a tax-classification defect on real documents, and it is the case that makes this row high priority. THE TWO ARE DISTINGUISHED BY READING THE WRITE PATH, not by looking at more rows: find every site that writes orders.place_of_supply and see what it reads. Start from status-transitions.ts, which builds order lines on PI confirmation, and from whatever seed file wrote these rows — day12.ts and day13.ts are the PI and order seeds. WHY THE BENIGN READING IS WEAK, recorded so nobody dismisses this on it: the obvious innocent explanation is that place_of_supply is an at-issue snapshot and the dealer's state was edited afterwards, which would make divergence legitimate. That reading does not hold here. Seed dealers are not edited after seeding — the seed writes them once and nothing mutates them — and a snapshot that had drifted by accident would diverge on a scattered subset, not on EXACTLY HALF. Exactly half points at a code path taken for one branch of a conditional and not the other. WHY THE DIAGNOSIS IS SEQUENCED BEFORE F.4: F.4 prints the tax block on the PDF, and that block renders CGST plus SGST for an intra-state document and IGST for an inter-state one. If this is real, F.4 would render THE WRONG TAX TYPE ON A LEGAL DOCUMENT, and it would do so on documents whose reference PDFs already encode the wrong type — so the error would look like a match. Diagnose before F.4 renders anything new. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: this is diagnosis first, then a decision. Do not fix and re-seed in the same motion. If case B holds it touches place-of-supply derivation, which ADR-012 governs and which CLAUDE.md section 10.1 names as a stop-and-ask surface; if case A holds it changes stored seeded money classification and needs the reference-render measurement set plus an explicit re-baseline decision. Cross-reference F.5a, which also concerns place of supply. SPLIT 2026-09-23: THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOW ITS OWN ROW, F.105, POSITIONED BEFORE F.101 IN THE ARRAY. This row keeps the measurement and owns the DECISION and any fix; F.105 owns the read-only investigation that establishes which of the two cases above holds. The split exists because this row's original sequencing instruction — diagnose before F.4 — was a sentence in a notes field, and nothing enforced it. Array position does. Do not start this row before F.105 reports: the two cases need different work, and which one applies is exactly what F.105 determines. DIAGNOSED AND RESCOPED 2026-09-23 BY F.105 — see docs/F105_AUDIT.md for the evidence. CASE A IS CONFIRMED; CASE B IS RULED OUT. The production path is correct on all three document types and structurally refuses to produce the bad value, so this row is bounded fixture corruption and NOT a live tax-classification defect. It no longer outranks F.101. THE DEFECT IS EIGHT HARDCODED LITERALS IN TWO SEED FILES: day12.ts:152 and :180, day13.ts:231 and :255 on place_of_supply, plus day12.ts:151 and :179, day13.ts:230 and :254 on tenant_state_at_issue. TWO SYMPTOMS, ONE ROW, BY OPERATOR RULING: the tenant_state_at_issue half was found by the same audit and folded in here rather than filed separately, because it is the same defect — the same hardcoded literals in the same inserts — with two symptoms that are separable only by which column you inspect. Two rows would have to be fixed together or the data stays wrong. THE SECOND SYMPTOM IS THE LARGER ONE: tenant sample is in KA (seeds/index.ts:75), so its 19 orders and 19 PIs store tenant_state_at_issue = 'MH' when the tenant is not in Maharashtra at all — BOTH SIDES of the inter-state comparison are wrong, the rows read intra-state, and the correct classification is KA against the ship-to's state, which is IGST on most of them. The demo tenant is clean on this axis only because it happens to be in MH. Quotations are clean on both columns. THE MEASURED SHAPE, replacing the inferred one: day12 writes 11 orders per tenant and day13 writes 8, both assigning ship-to round-robin while hardcoding the literal, so 19 per tenant are hardcoded; measured on the sample tenant, 2 of those 19 have an MH ship-to and coincidentally agree and 17 mismatch, giving 38 hardcoded, 4 coincidental and the 34 originally measured. The 34 is 17 order numbers times 2 tenants, not 34 distinct documents. WHAT THE BAD DATA ALREADY RENDERS: orders/[id]/page.tsx:74 feeds the stored place_of_supply into summariseDocument, so on ORD-2026-0003 — ship-to in AS, stored MH, one line at 18 percent on 50,000 — F.3's block renders CGST at 9 percent 4,500 and SGST at 9 percent 4,500 beside a header reading 0.00, where ADR-012 wants IGST at 18 percent 9,000. A wrong tax TYPE and a wrong AMOUNT on screen. F.4 will print the tax-type label from the same wrong columns. THE FILING'S RE-BASELINE COST IS REMOVED: this row assumed a corrected seed would move the 14 Chromium reference renders. IT WOULD NOT. There are no orders among the 14, and both reference PIs are clean on both columns for both tenants (PI-2026-0001 MH/MH and KA/MH, PI-2026-0002 TN/TN), and quotations, dispatches and payment receipts are unaffected. So the fix needs no deliberate re-baseline, which makes this row cheaper than filed. A THIRD, ADJACENT SEED DEFECT ON THE SAME INSERTS, in scope for whoever fixes this: day12 and day13 never set cgstAmount, sgstAmount or igstAmount at all, so all 38 orders and 38 PIs carry taxed line rows under zero-tax headers. That is what makes the ORD-2026-0003 divergence visible, and F.105 confirmed the divergence is a SEED artefact only — production always stores engine-computed totals over the same lines, and order-line money fields are immutable after creation, so no production document can render a summary its own header contradicts for this reason. NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the one production-reachable divergence of that shape is the discount allocation residual already documented at lib/tax/document-summary.ts:26-27, which is F.101. NO TEST ASSERTS EITHER INVARIANT — neither place_of_supply equals the ship-to's state nor tenant_state_at_issue equals tenant_settings.state — and verify-day-16.spec.ts:122-123 currently DEFENDS AGAINST this bad data in its row selection rather than asserting the rule, so a fix should consider whether that predicate can be relaxed. Finally, not a defect but worth correcting while in these files: day8.ts:163 and :173 comment their forcePlaceOfSupply overrides as inter-state vs MH, which holds for the demo tenant and not for sample (in KA), where QT-2026-0009 is forced to KA against a UP dealer and lands intra-state. RESEQUENCED 2026-09-23 TO INDEX 16, AHEAD OF F.4 AND F.101 — operator ruling. IT IS NOW DEMO-BLOCKING. The prospect is MAHARUDRA AGENCIES of Ponda, GOA (docs/client-evidence/5.png). A demo tenant seeded for a Goa client inherits precisely this defect: the hardcoded 'MH' makes tenant_state_at_issue wrong for any tenant not in Maharashtra — which is what it already does to the sample/KA tenant — and their orders would render CGST plus SGST where ADR-012 wants IGST, in front of them. F.105 measured the existing damage at 34 mismatching orders and 34 mismatching PIs. This is no longer housekeeping deferred behind engine work; it is the thing that must be true before F.106 seeds anything. COMPLETED 2026-09-23. THE FIX: eight literals removed, four per file — tenantStateAtIssue 'MH' and placeOfSupply 'MH' on both the performa-invoice insert and the order insert in each of day12.ts and day13.ts. The tenant state is now read from tenant_settings, following the day11.ts:175-179 precedent, and the place of supply is the SHIP-TO dealer's state per ADR-012 and CLAUDE.md section 5. Both seeds now select dealers.state, and a dealer with no state is filtered out rather than given a substitute, because inventing one is the defect being removed; the existing missing-prerequisites guard covers the new precondition. MEASURED, clean seed against clean seed, by reseeding with the pre-fix code on a truncated database and then with the fix: orders with place_of_supply not equal to the ship-to state went 34 to 0; PIs the same, 34 to 0; orders with tenant_state_at_issue not equal to the tenant's actual state went 19 to 0; PIs the same, 19 to 0. Corpus size is unchanged at 44 orders and 64 PIs, which rules out the fix having dropped rows — there are zero active dealers without a state, so the new filter removes nothing. THE 14 REFERENCE RENDERS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS THE CHANGE, MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED from F.105's prediction: rendered into a fresh directory before and after and the hashes diffed, with the pipeline then shown capable of reporting a difference by flipping one byte in a copied PDF and watching the same diff catch it. determinism-check prints MATCH with determinism-expected.json unmodified. Green: workers 60 tests, db 208, tax 81, plus lint, typecheck, check:paths, check:ids and plan:check. A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN FILING, AND TO docs/F105_AUDIT.md, MADE IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE FIX: this row and the audit both described the finding as 34 of 68 orders and as EXACTLY HALF, and this row inferred from that symmetry that it pointed at a code path taken for one branch of a conditional and not the other. THE DENOMINATOR WAS WRONG. It came from a development database holding more rows than one clean seed produces; pnpm db:seed TRUNCATEs at seeds/index.ts:108, and a clean run yields 44 orders and 64 PIs, not 68 and 89. Re-measured on a truncated database with the pre-fix code: 34 mismatching against 10 agreeing for orders, and 34 against 30 for PIs. The numerator 34 was right both times, as are every derivation, every write-site mapping and F.105's verdict, none of which depends on the denominator. What does not survive is the phrase exactly half and the inference it invited — the real shape is that 19 of each tenant's 22 orders are written by the two seed modules carrying the literal, and 17 of those 19 land on a non-MH ship-to. The symmetry was an artefact of the extra rows, which is why an absolute count measured against an unpinned database is weaker evidence than it looks. | F.106 | —     | Client demo seed — MAHARUDRA AGENCIES (Ponda, Goa): their products, dealers, Goa addresses and the PFI-2033 figures                                             | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-23 by operator ruling, together with the resequencing that put F.103, F.4 and this row ahead of F.101. WHY IT EXISTS: the prospect is MAHARUDRA AGENCIES, a solar distributor based in Ponda, GOA — established from docs/client-evidence/5.png and 4.png, which are screenshots of their current system (Swipe). A demo seeded with their own products, dealers and figures is what the signature meeting shows, which is why it now outranks engine work. WHAT TO SEED, read off the evidence: TENANT — MAHARUDRA AGENCIES, Maharudra House Bldg No. 225/1 Shop No. 1&2 Sapna Town, Ponda, GOA 403401; state GA; bank Bank of India, account 103720110000204, IFSC BKID0001037, branch TISK USGAO. PRODUCTS — 'Premier Energies 620wp topcon dcr', HSN 85414300, 15500.00 per NOS, GST 5 percent; and 'Solar Earthing Kit' (17.2MMX1MTR 3NOS, COPPER BONDED LA 1NOS, 15KG BFC BAG 2NOS, PIT COVER 6 inch 3NOS), HSN 85359090, 2350.00, GST 18 percent. DEALERS — a Goa ship-to at Canacona, GOA 403702, and a Maharashtra ship-to at Arihant, Gadhinglaj Ajara Road, Gadhinglaj, Kolhapur, MAHARASHTRA 416502. DOCUMENTS — PFI-2033 (2 lines: 36 NOS of the panel with a 2 percent line discount of 11718.00, plus 1 earthing kit; taxable 549190.00, CGST 13882.50, SGST 13882.50, total 576955.00) and tax invoice MA/26-27/1094 (26 NOS of the panel, no discount, taxable 403000.00, CGST 10075.00, SGST 10075.00, total 423150.00, ship-to Canacona Goa, 26 serials of the form NSMG2608000xxxx). THREE FINDINGS MEASURED BEFORE THIS ROW WAS FILED, ALL OPEN, NONE DECIDED — the first two mean the row's own instruction to seed 'the PFI-2033 figures' CANNOT BE SATISFIED EXACTLY, and the operator must choose what the demo shows. FINDING 1, THE DISCOUNT MODEL DIFFERS: the client applies discount PER LINE — PFI-2033's 11718.00 sits on line 1 only, with line 2 undiscounted — while Dealerlink has no per-line discount column at any grain and models discount only at DOCUMENT level, allocated proportionally across all lines. Measured through computeTax on the client's own line shapes: as an amount of 11718.00 the taxable comes to 548632.00 against the document's 549190.00 and the total to 576362.72 against 576955.00, a gap of 592.28; as a percent of 2 the taxable comes to 549143.00 and the total to 576899.54, a gap of 55.46. Neither reproduces the printed figures, and the proportional allocation moves line 2's taxable off 2350.00, which is visible on the page. FINDING 2, THE TAX TYPE DIVERGES ON THEIR OWN DOCUMENT: PFI-2033 ships to Gadhinglaj, Kolhapur, MAHARASHTRA while MAHARUDRA is in GOA, and the document nonetheless prints CGST 2.5 plus SGST 2.5 and CGST 9 plus SGST 9 — i.e. their system classifies by BILL-TO, which is in Goa. ADR-012 and CLAUDE.md section 5 make place of supply the SHIP-TO location for goods per IGST Act 2017 section 10, so Dealerlink would render that same document as IGST. Seeding it verbatim therefore shows the prospect a different tax type from their own paperwork, on their own data, in the demo. That is either a selling point or an objection depending on how it is introduced, and it is the operator's call which — it is NOT a defect in Dealerlink and must not be 'fixed' by weakening ADR-012. FINDING 3, AND IT CONFIRMS THE DEFERRAL: PFI-2033 is mixed-rate (5 and 18 percent) and discounted, which is the shape that can exhibit F.101's allocation residual — so it was measured rather than assumed, under both modellings, and the residual is 0.00 in each. The client demo therefore cannot exhibit F.101 either, which is consistent with the reason F.101 was deferred. DEPENDS ON F.103: this seed writes orders and PIs, and until day12.ts and day13.ts stop hardcoding 'MH' a Goa-tenant demo inherits exactly the defect F.105 measured at 34 mismatching orders and 34 PIs. That is why F.103 sits ahead of this row and not beside it. | F.101 | 35a   | computeTax allocates a document discount per line but derives discountAmount at document level, so the two disagree by a paisa                                  | ⏳     | —          | Found 2026-09-20 during F.3's A.1, by a property test over discounted documents rather than against the seed corpus. THE DEFECT, MEASURED: computeTax computes discountAmount at DOCUMENT level (compute.ts:36, round2 of the percent applied to the subtotal) but allocates it across lines as lineDiscount = round2(lineSubtotal \* discountRatio) PER LINE (compute.ts:54). Those two quantities are not equal. On a 4-rate inter-state document at 12.5% with line subtotals 24997 / 119925 / 83000 / 12450: discountAmount = 30046.50 while sum(lineDiscount) = 30046.51; taxableAmount = 210325.50 while sum(lineTaxable) = 210325.49; totalAmount = 226904.27 while sum(lineTotal) = 226904.26. On an undiscounted document every delta is 0.00, so the defect is specific to the discount path. THE ENGINE'S OWN DOCSTRING IS FALSE AS WRITTEN BECAUSE OF THIS: compute.ts:13-18 states the rounding model as "each line's subtotal is rounded to 2dp; the document subtotal is the SUM of those rounded line subtotals — so an invoice's printed line amounts always add up to the printed subtotal exactly". That promise holds for SUBTOTAL and fails for TAXABLE, DISCOUNT and TOTAL once a discount exists. The docstring should be corrected BY THIS TASK, not before it — correcting the words while the behaviour still contradicts them would make the file self-consistent and still wrong. WHY THIS IS SEQUENCED BEFORE F.4 AND NOT LATER: F.4 prints the HSN summary table and the document total ON ONE PAGE. On a discounted mixed-rate document that page would disagree with itself by a paisa — the rate-wise and HSN-wise rows would sum to one figure and the printed grand total would show another. A customer-facing tax document that does not add up on its face is worse than the one-paisa arithmetic suggests. THE REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE FIX, DECIDED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-09-20: keep the DOCUMENT-LEVEL discountAmount as the authority and allocate that exact amount across the lines so the allocation sums to it precisely — largest-remainder, distributing the residual paise deterministically. THIS MATTERS FOR A SPECIFIC REASON: it means the document scalars do not move, so every stored header on every historical document stays valid and no seeded or reference figure changes. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE IS THE OBVIOUS ONE: recomputing the document figure as the sum of per-line discounts. That would move discountAmount, taxableAmount and totalAmount on EVERY historical discounted document, which is F.99's failure mode exactly — a historical document reproducing differently from the way it was billed. Cross-reference F.99. WHAT F.3 DID INSTEAD, so this row is not re-derived: F.3 was forbidden to touch computeTax (its D-1 authorisation permits composing on the engine only), so it asserts the five reconciliation identities EXACTLY on undiscounted documents and CHARACTERISES the known delta on discounted ones, in packages/tax/tests/summary.test.ts. That characterisation test asserts a figure that is wrong by one paisa on purpose and says so in a comment; WHEN THIS TASK LANDS THAT TEST MUST FAIL, which is its job, and it must be updated deliberately rather than loosened. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: this changes money output in packages/tax on a protected surface, so it needs an explicit operator authorisation of the shape F.55, F.81 and F.84 used, plus a re-run of the full reference-render measurement set to prove no existing document moved — noting that no seeded document currently triggers the delta, because every discounted seeded document is single-rate with cleanly-dividing subtotals, so the seed corpus CANNOT demonstrate the fix and a new fixture or a property test is the only evidence available. CORRECTIONS AND DECISIONS, 2026-09-21, from prompt-drafter's read of the code plus operator rulings. FIRST, THE PREMISE IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND IS RESTATED AS "THREE BY CONSTRUCTION, FOUR BY MEASUREMENT". The row said document scalars must not move so stored headers stay valid. That is true of THREE of the seven stored header columns, not all seven. Immune by construction: subtotal (compute.ts:33), discount_amount (:36) and taxable_amount (:45), all derived at document level with no reference to the per-line allocation. CAN MOVE: cgst_amount, sgst_amount, igst_amount and total_amount, because the per-line taxes are computed ON lineTaxable (:64-69), summed into the document figures (:90-92), and total_amount is derived from those sums (:101). Re-allocating the discount changes lineTaxable on at least one line of any affected document, so those four are an empirical question with an instrument — quotation-engine-parity.test.ts asserts all seven stored columns and is the thing that would go red. Whether they move on any real document must be MEASURED on the day, not assumed either way. SECOND, THE SEQUENCING JUSTIFICATION IS REPLACED, because the original one was weaker than the truth. This row justified landing before F.4 by F.4's future HSN table printing beside the document total. The defect is ALREADY CUSTOMER-FACING on shipped quotations and PIs: apps/workers/src/templates-typst/quotation.typ:88 prints data.totalTaxable, which apps/workers/src/pdf/view-model.ts:122 computes as the SUM OF PER-LINE TAXABLES, while :102 prints data.taxableAmount, the DOCUMENT figure — both on the same page. On an affected document those two printed numbers differ by 0.01. No seeded document exhibits it today only because every discounted seeded document happens to have a zero allocation residual. THIRD, THE DEFECT IS REACHABLE WITH ORDINARY PRICES. A search over integer-rupee unit prices in a NARROW BAND CHOSEN BY THE AUTHOR found six mixed-rate discounted documents that exhibit a non-zero residual on the current engine. The cleanest: three units at 3331 rupees at 5 percent, three at 4165 at 18 percent, one at 8333 at 12 percent, discount 7.5 percent — discountAmount 2311.58 against sum(lineDiscount) 2311.59, and taxableAmount 28509.42 against sum(lineTaxable) 28509.41, a 0.01 residual on both, intra-state so CGST and SGST both move. THIS ROW MAKES NO CLAIM ABOUT FREQUENCY. The search was not exhaustive and the band was not representative, so nothing here establishes how common residuals are, and a later reader must not infer rarity from the fact that the seeded corpus has none. FOURTH, THE FIXTURE SHAPE IS DECIDED: NEW PRODUCTS WITH THEIR OWN SKUS, named fixture-only in the F.84 manner, appended after Chain D with their own counter allocation. NOT line-level price overrides, and the reason is specific: overrides route through the re-stamp-on-draft-save path that F.91 covers, which would add a second variable to a fixture whose entire purpose is to isolate one. The existing multi-rate catalogue cannot supply the prices — it holds 13325 and 13125 at 5 percent, 41500 at 12 percent, 4150 at 18 percent and 4165 at 3 percent — so new products are required regardless. THE FIXTURE MUST BE MEASURED TO EXHIBIT THE RESIDUAL BEFORE ANYTHING RELIES ON IT: a green run after the fix proves that nothing moved, NOT that the defect is gone, and only a document that fails before the change can demonstrate that it passes after. FIFTH, THE TIMING ARGUMENT, AND WHAT THE PRODUCTION COUNT DOES AND DOES NOT DECIDE. Whether any real tenant already holds a discounted multi-rate document is a production question that cannot be answered from the devcontainer: dealerlink-production-db refuses connections from here and its trusted-sources list contains exactly one entry, the production app itself, which is correct posture and was deliberately NOT changed. A read-only counting script was written for the DO app Console instead. A ZERO COUNT ESTABLISHES ONLY THAT TODAY IS CHEAP. It does not establish that the change is safe in general, and the window closes the moment one real tenant issues one discounted mixed-rate document — after which the four movable columns mean a re-render shows different GST than was billed, which is F.99 for real rather than in principle. SO THE COUNT DECIDES WHETHER F.99 HANDLING IS NEEDED ALONGSIDE F.101, NOT WHETHER F.101 PROCEEDS. A non-zero count does not block this task; it adds historical-document handling to it. THE PRODUCTION COUNT WAS SKIPPED, AND THE ZERO IS INFERRED FROM THE BUSINESS STATE RATHER THAN MEASURED — operator decision 2026-09-22. DO NOT READ IT AS A MEASURED ZERO. The inference: no tenant is live. UMA never used the system and the prospect has not signed, so production is expected to hold no real billed documents at all, and therefore no discounted multi-rate ones. That is a statement about who is using the product, not about what a query returned. Nothing was run against the production database. A read-only counting script was written and locally verified for the DO app Console — it prefers DATABASE_DIRECT_URL because DATABASE_URL connects as dealerlink_app, which is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, so a query through it returns 0 whether or not matching rows exist, and it refuses to draw a conclusion when its control sees zero documents of any kind. THAT SCRIPT LIVES ONLY IN THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED TO THE REPOSITORY. It can be rebuilt from this description if needed. THE EXIT CONDITION, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: IF ANY TENANT GOES LIVE BEFORE F.101 LANDS, THIS INFERENCE EXPIRES AND THE COUNT MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE THE DAY STARTS. The inference is only as good as the business state it rests on, and that state can change without anyone touching this row. CONSEQUENCE, ON THE INFERENCE AS IT STANDS: F.99 handling is NOT needed alongside F.101. THE TIMING ARGUMENT IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE REASON TO LAND THIS SOON: today is cheap, and the window closes the moment the first real tenant issues a discounted mixed-rate document — after which the four movable columns mean a re-render shows different GST than was billed, which is F.99 in fact rather than in principle. NOTE WHAT THIS DOES NOT AFFECT: the SEEDED residual sweep in the day's A.0 is a separate measurement and remains REQUIRED. It reads the dev corpus, it is the condition D-4 places on the whole day, and it must cover quotations, performa_invoices and orders. All 14 discounted seeded quotations are measured at 0.00 residual as of 2026-09-21; the eight discounted PIs and the orders are not yet measured. If any seeded residual is non-zero the day stops, regardless of anything inferred about production. DEFERRED 2026-09-23 to index 19, behind F.103, F.4 and F.106 — operator ruling, with the reason recorded so the ordering stays legible. NO SEEDED DOCUMENT EXHIBITS THE RESIDUAL — measured across all 24 discounted documents in all three document types during this task's A.0 (14 quotations, 8 PIs, 2 orders, every residual 0.00), and measured again on the client's own mixed-rate discounted PFI-2033 shape, also 0.00. So the demo cannot show the defect, and this row's own window closes only when a real tenant issues a discounted mixed-rate document, which is post-signature. A.0'S MEASUREMENTS ARE ALREADY TAKEN AND BANKED IN THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD — the residual sweep across all three document types with its executed falsifying control, the verification that three of the seven reference documents are discounted (QT-2026-0006 at 7.5 percent, QT-2026-0010 at 10 percent, PI-2026-0001 at 10 percent, confirming R-2's previously unverified inference), the 133 captured compute.test.ts expectation lines that form the STOP-condition baseline, and green pre-change baselines for the tax suite (81 tests) and the db suite (208 tests). DO NOT RE-DERIVE THEM WHEN THIS ROW RESUMES; re-take only what a changed tree invalidates. | F.6   | 37–39 | GST tax invoice document                                                                                                                                        | ⏳     | —          | Day 19 audit VERDICT: DOES NOT EXIST. Estimated 3.5 d against 2 d allocated. Hard-blocked on F.4 — TaxSummary is single-rate today. See docs/TAX_INVOICE_AUDIT.md §A.4. SCOPE CONFIRMED, Day 24 follow-up. The Day 19 'DOES NOT EXIST' verdict in docs/TAX_INVOICE_AUDIT.md:21 was RE-DERIVED from scratch after DEV.115 cast doubt on grep-based negative-existence claims, and it HOLDS. The re-audit was methodologically stronger than the original: it rests on AFFIRMATIVE ENUMERATIONS rather than empty searches — the complete list of `nextCounter` call sites, the complete list of `documentType:` literals, the complete list of `prefixes[...]` read keys, and full directory listings (50 pages, 23 schema files, 21 RLS policies, 18 migrations, 19 worker files). 'invoice is absent from this list I read in full' is a claim a silently-failing search tool cannot fake, which is exactly the property the re-audit was run to obtain. Confirmed absent: table/schema/migration/RLS, `'invoice'` allocation through `nextCounter`, write path, query helper, route or page, sidebar entry, worker template, role gate, and any test. Confirmed present as declaration-only placeholders: `generated_document_type` pg enum value (generated-document.ts:17, migration 0008), the `RenderableDocumentType` TS union arm (render-pdf.ts:28), the Zod arm in `renderPdfJobPayloadSchema` (packages/schemas/src/email.ts:57), and `doc_prefixes.invoice = 'INV'` (tenant-settings.ts:47, admin/constants.ts:19). The render-pdf throw claim is CONFIRMED with a correction to its wording: render-pdf.ts:54-65 is a NEGATIVE ALLOW-LIST of four implemented types, so `'invoice'` throws BY OMISSION rather than via an explicit `case 'invoice': throw`. TWO FINDINGS THE DAY 19 AUDIT MISSED, both of which change how F.6 is scoped: (1) THERE IS ALREADY A LIVE, ROLE-GATED, PERSISTING UI CONTROL NAMING A TAX INVOICE — apps/web/app/admin/tenants/[id]/tenant-detail-sections.tsx:817 renders an editable 'Tax invoice' prefix input in the operator tenant-detail screen, and saving it really does persist through `updateTenantDocPrefixes` (lib/actions/admin/update-tenant.ts:110). What it writes is a prefix STRING that no numbering code ever reads, so an operator can configure the prefix of a document that cannot be created. It is the single most likely reason for someone to believe the feature exists, and F.6 must either wire it up or label it. (2) THE PLACEHOLDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND CANNOT SIMPLY BE DELETED — `docPrefixesSchema` at apps/web/lib/admin/schemas.ts:70 makes the `invoice` key REQUIRED for any doc-prefix update, so removing it breaks an unrelated validated admin path. Touch that schema and the admin form together or not at all. BUILD ORDER from the re-audit, for whoever scopes this day: invoices + invoice_lines (+ status history) tables with migration, tenant_id, RLS and tenant_id-leading indexes; `'invoice'` allocated through `nextCounter` reading `prefixes['invoice']`; a `tenantAction` creating an invoice from a confirmed order, snapshotting lines and freezing `tenant_state_at_issue` / `place_of_supply`; query helpers; routes plus a sidebar entry; a worker template plus removing `'invoice'` from the render-pdf exclusion; role gating to Admin/Accounts per CLAUDE.md §6; tests. ROUND-OFF IS IN SCOPE FOR THIS TASK — operator ruling, Day 25 follow-up, and it OVERTURNS the Day 25 finding that recorded it as merely an untested case. Day 25 established correctly that no round-off line exists anywhere: `packages/tax` has no round-off field and performs only line-level `round2`; `TaxSummary.tsx` renders Subtotal → (discount) → IGST or CGST+SGST → Grand Total with no round-off row; and neither `quotations` nor `performa_invoices` has a round-off column. `packages/tax/src/round.ts` documents that as deliberate — 'NOT modelled by this engine … the quotation schema has no round-off column in Phase 1'. What Day 25 got wrong was the CONSEQUENCE: it concluded there was simply nothing to capture for a reference PDF. On the CLIENT path it is a functional gap, and the evidence is in the repository. EVIDENCE, verified first-hand from docs/client-evidence/ rather than relayed: (1) the client's documents total to WHOLE RUPEES — `5.png` is tax invoice MA/26-27/1094 with Taxable 4,03,000.00 + CGST 2.5% 10,075.00 + SGST 2.5% 10,075.00 = Total 4,23,150.00 and Amount Payable 4,23,150.00; `4.png` is PFI-2033 with Taxable 5,49,190.00 + CGST 13,671.00 + SGST 13,671.00 + CGST 211.50 + SGST 211.50 = Total 5,76,955.00; `4.png`'s sidebar lists a whole column of PI totals, every one a whole rupee (5,76,955.00 / 5,41,632.00 / 30,590.00 / 6,50,875.00 / 64,947.00 / 10,42,965.00 / 5,79,837.00 / 13,744.00). (2) THE DECISIVE LINK: `1.png` is the TallyPrime sales voucher MA/26-27/1079 for that same 13,744.00 document — items 8,917.50 + 3,712.00 = 12,629.50, SGST-OUTPUT 557.02, CGST-OUTPUT 557.02, which sums to 13,743.54, and it carries an explicit `ROUND OFFS 0.46` line to reach 13,744.00. So the round-off is not cosmetic: it is the entry that reconciles a whole-rupee document total against line-level tax arithmetic. (3) F.11 ALREADY REQUIRES IT — `docs/STAGE_F_BUILD_v3.md:211`, in the F.11 mapping table: 'Round-off ledger \| Screenshot 5 shows `ROUND OFFS 0.46`; without it the voucher will not balance.' WHY THIS LANDS ON F.6 RATHER THAN F.11: F.11 maps a round-off ledger that something must POST to. If the tax invoice never produces a round-off amount, F.11's mapping has no source value and the exported voucher cannot balance — so the producing end is F.6's, and F.6 must ship it or F.11 is built against a field that does not exist. SIZING: roughly +0.5 day on top of F.6's existing 3.5 d estimate (already over its 2 d allocation). The work is a `round_off` column on the invoice table plus its migration, a single grand-total adjustment computed ONCE on `totalAmount` — exactly as `round.ts` says it should be if introduced — a Round Off row in `TaxSummary.tsx`, and the value surfaced for F.11's export. SEQUENCING: stays inside F.6 at days 37-39, and inherits F.6's existing hard block on F.4 (multi-rate TaxSummary) — note `4.png` is itself a MULTI-RATE document, carrying both 2.5%/2.5% and 9%/9% lines, so the round-off row and the multi-rate summary land in the same component and should be built together rather than sequentially. PROTECTED SURFACE — STOP AND ASK: this touches `packages/tax` and a money column, both named in CLAUDE.md §10.1, so the grand-total round-off computation needs the operator conversation before implementation, not a drive-by addition. ALSO FIX WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: Day 25 captured no round-off reference PDF because none could exist; once the line ships, a reference must be captured for it — `docs/pdf-references/README.md` records that the matrix does NOT cover round-off and must not be read as if it does. A CITATION HAZARD FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS, worth fixing in F.60 or here: the screenshot numbering in `docs/STAGE_F_BUILD_v3.md` does NOT match the filenames in `docs/client-evidence/`. The spec's 'Screenshot 5' (ROUND OFFS 0.46, and the Tally item name `Premier NDCR TOPCON G12R 615 wp`) is file `1.png`; the spec's 'Screenshot 4' (`SALE @ 5% - CENTRAL` beside `SALES @ 18% - CENTRAL`) is file `2.png`. Anyone following a spec citation to a filename lands on the wrong image. THE ARITHMETIC, VERBATIM — operator instruction, recorded as an equation rather than paraphrased, because it is the single strongest piece of evidence in the case and a paraphrase loses the force of it. From `docs/client-evidence/1.png`, TallyPrime sales voucher `MA/26-27/1079`, party SAMARA POWER SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED, dated 1-Sep-26: items `Premier NDCR TOPCON G12R 615 wp` 1 NOS @ 8,917.50 = 8,917.50 and `PEDLER LB SWITCH-40A` 4 NOS @ 928.00 = 3,712.00, giving 12,629.50. Then: 12,629.50 + 557.02 (SGST-OUTPUT) + 557.02 (CGST-OUTPUT) = 13,743.54, against a document total of 13,744.00, closed by `ROUND OFFS 0.46`. WHAT THAT PROVES, and why it changes the classification: round-off RECONCILES A WHOLE-RUPEE DOCUMENT TOTAL AGAINST LINE-LEVEL TAX ARITHMETIC. It is a CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT, not a display convention. Without the adjustment the two figures disagree by 46 paise and the voucher does not balance — which is precisely what `docs/STAGE_F_BUILD_v3.md` says under F.11's mapping table. Corroborating that the 13,744.00 total is the client's own and not a Tally artefact: the same figure appears in the Swipe PFI list in `4.png`, alongside a column of other totals that are ALL whole rupees. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT WITH F.4 — recorded on BOTH tasks, not as a one-sided note: the round-off row and F.4's multi-rate GST summary land in the SAME component, `apps/workers/src/templates-typst/quotation.typ:97-110`, which today renders only Subtotal → (discount) → IGST or CGST+SGST → Grand Total at a single rate. `4.png` is itself a mixed-rate document — CGST 2.5% 13,671.00 and SGST 2.5% 13,671.00 alongside CGST 9.0% 211.50 and SGST 9.0% 211.50 — so the real client document needs BOTH changes at once. Building them sequentially means editing the same component twice and re-capturing the same reference PDFs twice. Build them together. F.6 is already hard-blocked on F.4; this constraint is stronger than the block, because it says they should be ONE piece of work rather than two in order. CORRECTION, 2026-09-17, from docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md §1.2 and §6 (merged, PR #36): TWO THINGS IN THIS NOTE POINTED AT DEAD CODE AND ARE CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN PORTED FORWARD. (1) THE COMPONENT. `apps/workers/src/templates/_components/TaxSummary.tsx` has been unreachable at runtime since ADR-015 (Day 27). `render-pdf.ts:25-33` imports only the four `load*PdfData` loaders; the four `build*Html` entry points have zero call sites; `TaxSummary`'s single import sits inside `renderQuotationHtml`, whose only live caller is a unit test. The live single-rate totals block is `apps/workers/src/templates-typst/quotation.typ:97-110`, and `templates-typst/performa-invoice.typ:15,22` imports it verbatim, so quotation and PI share ONE site. Every remaining bare mention of "TaxSummary" in this note refers to the decommissioned component. (2) THE ROUND-OFF INSERTION POINT — RESOLVED. This note previously said the work includes "a Round Off row in `TaxSummary.tsx`". There were two competing records of where the round-off row goes; `apps/workers/src/templates-typst/_lib/chrome.typ:337-346` IS THE AUTHORITATIVE ONE and this note is the one that was wrong. chrome.typ:337-346 is a comment block in live, on-render-path code that states: "ROUND-OFF INSERTION POINT. The whole-rupee round-off adjustment line is NOT implemented in Phase 1 and must not be added here — it is F.6's, it has tax consequences, and it is not a rendering concern. Insert it as one more pair in `rows` immediately before the rule below and nothing else moves: ("Round Off", money(data.roundOff))". READ THAT MECHANISM PRECISELY, because the comment's location and the edit's location are different files: `totals-block(words:, rows:, grand:)` at chrome.typ:347 is CALLER-DRIVEN — chrome.typ:363-366 renders whatever pairs it is handed and the 2px rule is at chrome.typ:369 — so NO EDIT TO chrome.typ IS REQUIRED. The row is added to the `rows:` argument built by the caller, i.e. in `apps/workers/src/templates-typst/quotation.typ` between line 107 (the `})` closing the inter/intra conditional) and line 108 (the `),` closing the `rows:` argument), immediately after the last tax row and before `grand: data.totalAmount` at :109. That is also exactly where F.4's multi-rate rows land, which is the mechanical reason the two tasks are one piece of work. CONFIRMED STILL TRUE by the same audit: no round-off row exists in any template, any on-screen block, or `packages/tax`; and no `round_off` column exists on any totals-bearing table — established by enumerating the columns of `quotations` (quotation.ts:39-129), `performa_invoices` (performa-invoice.ts:43-137), `orders` (order.ts:47-130), `payments`, `payment_allocations` and the three dispatch tables in full, not by searching for the word. The four on-screen totals blocks would take the row at: summary-card.tsx between :96 and :97; quotations/[id]/page.tsx between :258 and :259; pi/[id]/page.tsx immediately before :256; orders/[id]/page.tsx between :214 and :215. | F.11  | 46–48 | Tally mapping configuration module                                                                                                                              | ⏳     | —          | RESCOPED 2026-09-19 BY OPERATOR RULING, during F.3's pre-day scoping. F.11 CONSUMES F.3's GROUPING COMPUTATION, NOT lib/reports/gst-summary.ts. The earlier assumption was that F.3 would add a rate-wise and HSN-wise axis to the GST Summary report and that F.11 would read that report's query. It will not. THE REASON IS A CONTRACT, NOT A LIMITATION: gst-summary.ts:8-12 states that every figure is the order's STORED taxable_amount and cgst/sgst/igst_amount and that the report MUST NOT call @dealerlink/tax — verified 2026-09-19, the module has no such import. That contract is CORRECT AND STAYS: the report shows what was BILLED, not what the engine would compute today, which is precisely what a GSTR-1 base must do. Consequently the report's rate axis can carry taxable value and order counts but NOT rate-wise tax amounts, since producing those would require recomputation the contract forbids. F.11 therefore routes through F.3's computation in packages/tax, which does derive tax through computeTax and reconciles to the stored headers. WHAT TO CHECK WHEN F.11 IS SCHEDULED: that the axis F.11 maps to Tally ledgers (SALE @ 5% - LOCAL and the rest) comes from F.3's byRate/byHsn output, and that nothing in F.11 re-derives tax from the report's query. See also the per-line tax storage row filed the same day, which is why every consumer including F.11 recomputes at all. | F.55  | —     | packages/tax `GstRate` union omits 3% — type-versus-runtime mismatch on a protected surface                                                                     | ✅     | 2026-09-18 | `packages/tax/src/types.ts:7` declares `export type GstRate = 0 \| 5 \| 12 \| 18 \| 28;` — no 3. The database disagrees: `products_gst_rate_chk`, `quotation_lines_gst_rate_chk`, `performa_invoice_lines_gst_rate_chk` and `order_lines_gst_rate_chk` all read `IN (0, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28)` (packages/db/src/schema/product.ts:72, quotation.ts:171, performa-invoice.ts:175, order.ts:172), and CLAUDE.md §5 states the allowed rates as `0, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28`. So a 3% row is legal in Postgres, legal per the spec, and unrepresentable in the tax engine's own type. The doc comment above the union also cites the wrong section — it says 'per CLAUDE.md §6' where the rates live in §5. WHY THIS MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: F.3 (multi-rate tax summary, days 35) groups and keys by rate, and CLAUDE.md §5 already warns that `gst_rate` arrives from the driver as a STRING ('18' vs '18.00'), so grouping must normalise to a number first. A union that silently excludes 3 is the second half of that trap — a 3% group would be dropped or mistyped rather than double-counted, which is harder to notice. `packages/tax` is a PROTECTED SURFACE under CLAUDE.md §10.1 and docs/STAGE_F_BUILD_v3.md §9: widening the union changes the exhaustiveness of every `switch` and every `Record<GstRate, …>` that consumes it, so this needs its own scoped change with the tax suite re-run, not a drive-by edit. Raised Day 24 during F.52; deliberately NOT fixed that day. Sequence it BEFORE F.3. UPDATED 2026-09-17 — THE MISMATCH IS WORSE THAN THIS ENTRY RECORDS, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN READ. This entry describes a TYPE-level gap at `packages/tax/src/types.ts:7`. It is also a RUNTIME gap: `packages/tax/src/compute.ts:7` declares `const VALID_GST_RATES = [0, 5, 12, 18, 28];` and `compute.ts:135-140` THROWS on anything outside it. Executed against the real engine source on 2026-09-17 (operator asked for measurement, not inference), a 3% line returns: `THREW TaxComputationError code=INVALID_GST_RATE: Line L1: gstRate 3 not in {0,5,12,18,28}`, while 5, 12 and 18 all compute normally. So a 3% rate is not merely unrepresentable in the type — it is INSERTABLE BY ANY ROUTE THAT BYPASSES THE ZOD LAYER (the DB CHECK accepts it; verified on a live Postgres 16.15 the same day by inserting `'3'`, which stores and returns as `3.00`) AND THEN UN-RENDERABLE, because the PDF path calls `computeTax`. THE OMISSION IS NOT IN ONE PLACE BUT NINE, which is the complete enumeration of rate-list constants in the repo and the reason this is not a one-line fix: packages/tax/src/types.ts:7, packages/tax/src/compute.ts:7, packages/schemas/src/product.ts:4, packages/schemas/src/quotation.ts:42, apps/workers/src/templates/quotation.tsx:46, apps/workers/src/templates/performa-invoice.tsx:35, and the two `<select>` option arrays at apps/web/app/(app)/catalog/new/new-product-form.tsx:125 and apps/web/app/(app)/catalog/[id]/product-detail-sections.tsx:259. None contains 3. ALSO MEASURED, and relevant to whoever widens the union: `compute.ts:135` is `VALID_GST_RATES.includes(line.gstRate)`, an `includes()` on a NUMBER array with no adjacent `Number()`. Handing it the raw DB string throws too — `THREW TaxComputationError code=INVALID_GST_RATE: Line L1: gstRate 18.00 not in {0,5,12,18,28}`. No traced call path does that today (all five `as GstRate` sites coerce first), so this is a fail-safe backstop rather than a live defect — it fails loudly rather than silently double-counting — but it means the guard depends on every caller coercing, and that property should survive the change. NO FIX ATTEMPTED: `packages/tax` is a protected surface under CLAUDE.md §10.1. Reported only. Source: docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md §3.4 and §4.3. This entry's existing "Sequence it BEFORE F.3" instruction stands and is reinforced. CROSS-REFERENCE ADDED 2026-09-17: the sentence earlier in this note that reads "CLAUDE.md §5 already warns that `gst_rate` arrives from the driver as a STRING ('18' vs '18.00'), so grouping must normalise to a number first" RESTATES A FRAMING THAT HAS SINCE BEEN CORRECTED, and is left in place only because this note is a record. The string premise holds. What does NOT hold is the implied failure mode: `'18'` and `'18.00'` cannot form two groups from a read of the four `decimal(5, 2)` rate columns, because Postgres returns one canonical `'18.00'` for every written form (measured 2026-09-17; DEV.135, `docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md` §8.1). The real hazard is a DB-read rate string compared against a hand-written literal. `CLAUDE.md` §5 was rewritten accordingly under F.82, and is the single source. Read it there before acting on the sentence above. CORRECTION 2026-09-17, FROM `docs/F55_AUDIT.md`: THE COUNT IS EIGHT, NOT NINE. The open question above is now settled: shape-only validation, not a corrected list and not tenant-configurable data. THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE CHOICE, and the operator's instruction is that it be recorded because it is stronger than the staleness argument and it generalises. In the operator's terms: the tenant's accountant is unavailable until a deal closes, so ANY DESIGN THAT NEEDS TO KNOW THEIR SLAB SET CANNOT BE BUILT. Option B needs it — a tenant-configurable list has to be seeded with that tenant's rates before it is usable, and a default that is wrong for the tenant is the hardcoded list again with an extra table. Option A is THE ONLY OPTION THAT DOES NOT ASK: shape validation makes no claim about which rates exist, so it can be built and shipped before anyone has spoken to an accountant, and the tenant's own classification — which is what a rate on a product IS — remains entirely theirs to assert. WHY THIS GENERALISES AND THE STALENESS ARGUMENT DOES NOT. The staleness argument is about this codebase and this Council: a hardcoded list went stale twice, nobody noticed, and R8 (the procedure written to handle exactly that) went stale with it. Real, but bounded — it argues for maintaining the list better. The commercial argument is structural and applies to EVERY FUTURE TENANT: onboarding cannot depend on a fact only the tenant's accountant possesses, because at onboarding time that accountant is not reachable. Any validation that encodes a statutory claim therefore puts a blocking external dependency inside the provisioning path. That is a product constraint, not a code-quality preference, and it does not expire when this particular slab question is settled. All four rate columns are `decimal(5,2)` — `packages/db/src/schema/product.ts:38`, `quotation.ts:157`, `performa-invoice.ts:162`, `order.ts:155` — so Postgres normalises on write and the driver returns ONE canonical spelling for every input form. Verified on a real Postgres 16.15 through the application's own stack (postgres.js 3.4.9 + drizzle-orm 0.45.2), using the migration's exact DDL: rows written as `'18'`, `'18.00'`, `18` and `'18.0'` ALL read back as the string `'18.00'`, and `new Set([the '18'-written row, the '18.00'-written row]).size` is 1, not 2. Two rows cannot disagree, so a rate-keyed grouping over these columns cannot split or double-count on spelling. Full method and output: `docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md` §8.1; reasoning and why it was not folded in: DEV.135. WHAT THE REAL HAZARD IS, and why this is a correction rather than a deletion: the string premise in §5 is CORRECT and must stay — the driver does return a string, not a number (`typeof string`, measured). What is wrong is only the named failure mode. The live hazard is a DB string compared against a NON-DB string — a React `<option value>`, a hand-written literal, a form default — not two DB values disagreeing with each other. `docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md` §3.3 enumerated the complete 12-member set of comparison/keying sites in the repo and found exactly one live exposure, and it is of that second kind: the controlled `<select>` at `apps/web/app/(app)/catalog/[id]/product-detail-sections.tsx:255`, whose options render as `'0' '5' '12' '18' '28'` while the value arriving from `apps/web/lib/queries/products.ts:14,63` is `'18.00'`, so `['0','5','12','18','28'].includes('18.00')` is `false` and no option matches. Notably the three `Set`-by-rate sites §5's wording actually points at — `apps/workers/src/templates/quotation.tsx:234`, `apps/workers/src/templates/performa-invoice.tsx:161`, `apps/web/app/(app)/quotations/_components/summary-card.tsx:38` — ALL already normalise. WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO SCHEDULE: a warning that names the wrong mechanism sends the reader to guard the wrong line. Someone building F.3's rate-wise grouping will dutifully `Number()` a value that was never going to collide, and will not think about the comparison that actually breaks, because §5 does not describe it. SCOPE: a prose correction to `CLAUDE.md` §5 (main-thread-only per §10.4) — keep the "returns as a STRING" premise, replace the two-groups failure mode with the DB-string-vs-literal one, and cite the measurement. ALSO IN SCOPE, because it carries the same imprecise framing to whoever picks it up first: `F.55`'s notes restate §5's "('18' vs '18.00') ... second half of that trap" wording; it should gain a pointer to this correction. Consider whether this belongs folded into `F.56` (CLAUDE.md accuracy pass) instead of standing alone — F.56 enumerates DOC_AUDIT findings 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 and the CLAUDE.md half of 11, and does NOT currently cover this; merging the two is an operator call. NOT A CODE CHANGE: `packages/tax` and the four columns are untouched by this task. Raised by closeout verification on 2026-09-17 after DEV.135 was written, on the grounds that §11.2's remedy is a row OR a deviation entry and only the entry existed. CLOSED 2026-09-17, operator-instructed. `CLAUDE.md` §5's `gstRate` bullet was rewritten to name the measured mechanism. It now states three things the old wording did not: (a) the string premise still holds and normalising is still required, (b) what CANNOT happen — the four rate columns are `decimal(5, 2)`, so Postgres returns one canonical `'18.00'` for every written form and a rate-keyed grouping over them cannot split or double-count, with the note that the old warning "has been repeated into day prompts since Day 20, pointing every reader at the wrong line" (operator's own account), and (c) what DOES happen — a DB-read rate string compared against a hand-written literal, shown as `['0','5','12','18','28'].includes('18.00') // false`, with the live defect at `apps/web/app/(app)/catalog/[id]/product-detail-sections.tsx:255` named as a real shipped instance rather than a hypothetical, and the one-line rule "Guard the boundary between a DB value and a literal, not the boundary between two DB values." Provenance cites DEV.135, `docs/F3_F4_AUDIT.md` §3.3 and §8.1, and the measurement stack (Postgres 16.15 + postgres.js 3.4.9 + drizzle-orm 0.45.2). ALSO CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE, because leaving it would have recreated the problem this task exists to fix: `docs/STAGE_F_BUILD_v3.md:439-440` §9 Standing guardrails carried a one-line restatement of the same wrong mechanism, in the block read before every build day. Per the F.80 operator ruling — one authoritative source, pointers rather than duplicated reasoning — it was converted into a POINTER to `CLAUDE.md` §5 rather than a second corrected copy, on the grounds that two copies of the same reasoning drift and fail the same way and more quietly (DEV.132, DEV.133, DEV.134). NOT CHANGED: the `0, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28` allowed-rates sentence at the end of the §5 bullet. It is accurate as a statement about the `*_gst_rate_chk` constraints, which is what it says. That the APPLICATION rejects 3% — nine rate-list constants omit it and `computeTax` throws `INVALID_GST_RATE`, measured — remains F.55's subject and was deliberately not folded in here.
