| F.84  | —     | Seed a 3% product and a 3%-bearing document, plus the render and request coverage F.55 deferred                                                                 | ✅     | 2026-09-19 | HARD-BLOCKED ON F.55. Filed 2026-09-17, operator instruction, at the same time as the F.81/F.55 ordering decision. F.81 deliberately seeds NO 3% product: F.55 records that nine separate rate-list constants omit 3 while the DB CHECK accepts it, and that `computeTax` throws `INVALID_GST_RATE` on a 3% line (measured 2026-09-17). A 3% product seeded before F.55 would be insertable and then un-renderable. THE SEQUENCING RATIONALE, which is the reason this is a separate row rather than part of either task: F.55 widens a union on a PROTECTED SURFACE (`packages/tax`, CLAUDE.md §10.1), and widening a type without a fixture that exercises it leaves the change unverified. So F.55 lands first, then this row adds the fixture, so the widened union acquires something that can exercise it on the same day. Scope when it runs: one product at 3% with its own HSN, and at least one document carrying it, following whatever module placement F.81 established. ROUNDING NOTE, MEASURED 2026-09-17 and directly relevant here: 3% is one of only two rates in the allowed set `{0, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28}` that is ROUNDING-SENSITIVE under the intra-state CGST/SGST split. CGST at half of 3% is 1.5%, and 1.5% of an integer line subtotal lands off 2dp for 50% of integers (2000/4000 sampled); the same is true of 5% (CGST 2.5%), while 0, 12, 18 and 28 are exact on every integer subtotal because their halves are whole percentages. Whatever parity decision F.81 takes about how stored totals are produced will therefore apply here too, and for the same reason. SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-09-17, FROM `docs/F55_AUDIT.md` section 5: AS SCOPED, THIS FIXTURE WOULD NOT PROVE 3 PERCENT WORKS END TO END. The audit enumerated the 18 surfaces a 3 percent value must traverse and what covers each today. This row's scope — "one product at 3% with its own HSN, and at least one document carrying it" — reaches the DATA layers and misses the RENDER and REQUEST layers, and the render and request layers are precisely where the unguarded throws live. WHAT IT REACHES: the products CHECK accepting 3 (demonstrated by the insert succeeding); the tax engine, via `quotation-engine-parity.test.ts` re-running `computeTax` over every seeded `QT-%` quotation, provided the 3 percent document is a quotation whose totals are computed with `computeTax` as `multi-rate.ts` does; the quotation-line, PI-line and order-line CHECKs if the chain extends; and a corpus-shape assertion in `packages/db/tests/`. WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH: (1) THE PDF SNAPSHOTS. A seeded document does not enter `apps/workers/scripts/typst-matrix.json` by existing — the matrix is a hand-maintained list of 14 labelled cases, and F.81's own multi-rate documents are already absent from it. So `toGstRate` in `apps/workers/src/templates/quotation.tsx:49` and `performa-invoice.tsx:37`, which throw a PLAIN `Error` on an unexpected rate, stay unexercised. (2) THE ZOD REFINEMENTS at `packages/schemas/src/product.ts:4` and `quotation.ts:42`, and the browser preview at `apps/web/lib/quotation/preview.ts`. A seed inserts through Drizzle and bypasses Zod entirely, so nothing in a seed proves those refinements accept 3. (3) THE SERVER ACTIONS AND THE `<select>` ARRAYS — `createProduct`, the catalogue form, `convertQuotationToPi`. The two `<select>` arrays in particular can be widened or left narrow without any seed noticing. CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: this row remains correctly blocked on F.55, and its own stated rationale — "widening a type without a fixture that exercises it leaves the change unverified" — is sound and unchanged. What changes is that the fixture described here is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and whoever writes the F.55 spec should decide whether the render-layer and request-layer coverage belongs in F.55 itself, in this row with a widened scope, or in a third row. Not decided here. ONE THING THIS ROW ALREADY GETS RIGHT, confirmed: its rounding note. 3 percent intra-state splits to CGST and SGST at 1.5 percent each, and 1.5 percent of an integer subtotal is off 2dp for half of all integers — the same property F.81 measured and documented for 5 percent, where the seeded Chain A document carries CGST 10073.01 per-line against 10073.00 document-level. So a 3 percent fixture inherits an already-observed rounding behaviour rather than a hypothetical one. RE-SCOPED AND UNBLOCKED 2026-09-18, on F.55's completion. F.55 landed, so `computeTax`, both Zod layers, the four DB CHECKs and the two PDF loaders now all accept any shape-valid rate — 3 percent included. The HARD-BLOCKED ON F.55 condition is discharged. THE SCOPE IS NOW WIDER THAN THIS ROW ORIGINALLY STATED, and F.55 deliberately did not do the extra part. F.55 lands with acceptance criterion 5 unmet by design (D-1): it ships no render check and no matrix entry, because seed data is the only thing that can move a rendered document and mixing it with a validation change would have made the byte-comparison unattributable. So F.84 now carries THREE things rather than one: (1) THE FIXTURE, as originally scoped — a product at 3 percent with its own HSN and at least one document carrying it, following F.81's module placement; (2) THE RENDER CHECK, which F.55's day prompt A.8 specifies and sizes — a new test in `apps/workers/tests/` rendering a seeded document at a novel rate through the production chain (`loadQuotationPdfData` then `buildViewModel` then `renderTypstPdf`, the chain `pdf-snapshots.test.ts` already uses), asserting the loader does not throw and the extracted text carries the rate and its half (3 percent yields a `1.5%` half-rate label). NO GOLDEN FILE AND NO MATRIX ENTRY: `pdf-snapshots.test.ts` reads a reference PDF for every matrix case, the Chromium pipeline that produced those is gone (F.83), and F.81's ruling assigns the first Typst golden file to F.4; (3) THE REQUEST-LAYER CHECK — the only mechanical route to `createProduct` at a novel rate is Playwright, in a NEW `verify-day-*.spec.ts`, never `critical-path.spec.ts`, which is protected. Note that F.55 already shipped `apps/web/tests/e2e/verify-day-f55.spec.ts` covering the catalogue form at 40 percent and the D-6 warning, so the remaining request-layer gap is narrower than it was: what F.84 adds is the same coverage at 3 percent on a seeded document, end to end through quotation, PI and order. WHY THE RENDER PATH STILL NEEDS PROVING even though F.55 deleted the loaders' rate gates: deleting a gate is not the same as demonstrating the path works at a rate that never flowed through it, and `docs/GST_RATE_MODEL_AUDIT.md` section 3.4 established that everything downstream of those gates is rate-agnostic by reading rather than by execution. REQUEST-LAYER SCOPE NARROWED 2026-09-19, operator instruction, so this row describes the WORK rather than its filed shape. The re-scope note above lists a request-layer check as one of three items. Part of it has since shipped: F.55 delivered `apps/web/tests/e2e/verify-day-f55.spec.ts`, whose three cases assert (1) the rate control on `/catalog/new` is a numeric input — `toHaveAttribute('type', 'number')` — and that no hardcoded slab option renders, (2) a product SAVES at 40 percent through `createProduct`, with the D-6 warning appearing on the first click and the save completing on the second, reaching `/catalog/<id>`, and (3) a rate already in the catalogue produces NO warning, which is the control that distinguishes a correct warning from one that fires on everything. WHAT THAT LEAVES, and it is narrower than filed: the catalogue form at a novel rate is now covered, and so is the D-6 affordance. WHAT REMAINS is 3 percent specifically, on a SEEDED document, through quotation then PI then order — i.e. the document chain rather than the product master. The distinction matters because F.55's spec section 5 item 1 requires end-to-end reach and the catalogue form is only the first hop: `verify-day-f55.spec.ts` creates a product and stops there. Nothing yet drives a 3 percent rate through `createQuotation`, `convertQuotationToPi` or the order path at the request layer, and `convert-quotation-to-pi.ts` is the one production path that reaches `computeTax` with NO Zod layer in front of it (`docs/F55_AUDIT.md` section 2), so it is the hop most worth covering. DO NOT ADD TO `critical-path.spec.ts`, which is protected; a new `verify-day-*.spec.ts` is the route, as F.55 used. ALSO NOTE, so the next reader does not re-derive it: this is now a FIXTURE-AND-COVERAGE row, not a validation row. F.55 made 3 percent shape-valid at every layer — the four DB CHECKs are `gst_rate >= 0`, both Zod sites share `gstRateSchema`, the engine's guard is shape-only, and both PDF-loader read gates are gone. So nothing here needs to widen a type, a constraint or a schema, and if anything during the day appears to, that contradicts the premise and is a finding rather than a task. CORRECTIONS 2026-09-19, at the point the day prompt was approved. TWO THINGS IN THIS ROW WERE WRONG AND ARE FIXED RATHER THAN LEFT TO MISLEAD. FIRST, A CITATION: this row cited "F.55's spec section 5.1" in the re-scope paragraph, and `docs/F55_SPEC.md` has no section 5.1 — the end-to-end requirement is item 1 under `## 5. Acceptance`. Corrected in place. A citation is read as authority, which is ruling 6's point applied to a section anchor rather than to an id. SECOND, THE REQUEST-LAYER SCOPE OVERSTATED WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS, AND THE WORDING WAS THE OPERATOR'S OWN. The narrowing paragraph above says the remaining work is 3 percent "through quotation then PI then order". The operator has stated that this wording was ASPIRATIONAL rather than evidenced, and the day prompt's D-6 settles it as the two hops that actually lack a schema in front of `computeTax`: the browser preview at `apps/web/lib/quotation/preview.ts:83` and `apps/web/lib/actions/pi/convert-quotation-to-pi.ts:86`, both named in `docs/F55_AUDIT.md` section 2. WHY THE ORDER HOP IS EXCLUDED, AND THE ORIGINAL REASON FOR EXCLUDING IT WAS WRONG. The reason offered was that `createQuotation` and the order hop "have schemas and are covered". Measured on 2026-09-19: `createQuotation` does — `apps/web/lib/actions/quotations/create-quotation.ts:31` wires `createQuotationSchema`. But THE ORDER HOP'S SCHEMA DOES NOT SEE THE RATE AT ALL. `confirmPi` is a `tenantAction` carrying `confirmPiSchema`, and `packages/schemas/src/performa-invoice.ts:62` is `z.object({ id: z.string().uuid() })` — the PI id and nothing else. The order lines take `gstRate: l.gstRate` copied verbatim out of `performa_invoice_lines` in `apps/web/lib/actions/pi/status-transitions.ts`, never through Zod. So the order hop is NOT rate-guarded — and the corrected reason is stronger than the original: it performs NO rate validation whatsoever, so there is no gate there that could reject 3 percent. It is a pure copy. The two hops D-6 does cover are different in kind, because they reach a real validator with nothing in front of it. Excluding the order hop because it is INERT is sound; excluding it because it is GUARDED would have been a false statement about the code. BUILT 2026-09-19, PR pending. Ran from docs/F84_DAY_PROMPT.md, status APPROVED, D-1 to D-8 settled; no ninth decision arose. Three things shipped rather than one, per DEV.139's closeout. (1) THE FIXTURE: product MR-ASSAY-KIT on HSN 71131900 at '3.00', named "Assay Reference Kit (fixture-only, non-solar)" so no reader takes it as a statutory claim about solar goods. Chains C and D appended to packages/db/src/seeds/multi-rate.ts strictly after Chain B per D-1, for both tenants. Chain C is a single-rate intra-state quotation converting to a PI; Chain D is an accepted quotation with no PI, which is what the request-layer spec converts for itself. All totals from computeTax via serializeOutput; nothing under packages/tax changed. (2) THE RENDER CHECK: apps/workers/tests/three-percent-render.test.ts, 4 cases. (3) THE REQUEST LAYER: apps/web/tests/e2e/verify-day-f84.spec.ts, 3 cases, driving the two hops that reach computeTax with no Zod in front of them (the browser preview and convert-quotation-to-pi), per D-6. F.55's ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 5 IS NOW MET. DEV.139 recorded it unmet by design because seed data is the only thing that can move a rendered document and mixing it with a validation change would have made the byte comparison unattributable. three-percent-render.test.ts closes it: loadQuotationPdfData -> buildViewModel -> renderTypstPdf on a seeded 3% document, no throw, extracted text carrying 3%, CGST1.5% and SGST1.5% with no IGST. The preconditions that make the criterion satisfiable at all were absent from both source documents and are recorded as DEV.140. R-4's CORRECTION, which supersedes this row's older SCOPE CORRECTION paragraph. That paragraph lists "the products CHECK accepting 3" among the things this fixture demonstrates. F.55 already covers it, at packages/db/tests/gst-rate-invariant.test.ts:72,149-168 and packages/db/tests/dealers.test.ts:176-193. What the fixture adds that nothing else can is a PERSISTED 3% document, which packages/db/tests/quotation-engine-parity.test.ts:51-101 (it sweeps every seeded QT- quotation), the render path and the corpus paths can see. Read the narrower claim, not the older one. COVERAGE STOPS AT THE PI. Per D-2 and D-6 the fixture stops at the PI, so 3% coverage does NOT reach orders. There is no 3% order row, no 3% dispatch and no 3% tax invoice. A later task needing a 3% order is a SEPARATE FIXTURE ADDITION with its own counter allocation, not a tweak to this one, because inserting a row mid-chain is what the append-after-Chain-B discipline forbids. Nobody should read "3% coverage exists" as reaching further than quotation and PI. D-3's ADDRESSING HELD, AND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. D-3 overruled the drafter and kept resolveDocument addressing by document number on the grounds that append-after-Chain-B is the protection. F.81 holds QT-2026-0016 (Chain A) and QT-2026-0017 (Chain B); F.84 took QT-2026-0018, QT-2026-0019 and PI-2026-0032. Every matrix-addressed document still resolves to the same entity with the same totals (QT-2026-0001, QT-2026-0006, QT-2026-0010, PI-2026-0001, PI-2026-0002, PAY-2026-0007, DSP-2026-0005), and the 14 text snapshots passing is the stronger form of that check since a moved address would fail them. CONTROLS EXECUTED, NOT DESIGNED. A.3 selective deletion: with the 3% rows removed, five corpus cases go red and seven stay green, so the suite asserts on the rate rather than on the seed's existence. A.4 wrong document: pointed at single-rate 18% QT-2026-0001, two cases fail; that control is now permanent rather than a one-off, because the fourth case in the file asserts an 18% document carries CGST9% and not CGST1.5%. D-4's rounding property carries an even-subtotal control: Chain C's odd subtotals 12495 and 24997 give per-line CGST 562.39 against 562.38 document-level, while an even pair (8332, 14280) agrees at 339.16/339.18 and could not discriminate. THE THREE MEASUREMENTS. (1) TEXT against the Chromium reference contract: 14 reference-document cases plus 3 property cases, enumerated by name from a verbose run rather than counted, all 17 pass. That value is a HARDCODED SQL LITERAL. It is NOT derived from `packages/db/src/seeds/clock.ts`, where `SEED_EPOCH_ISO` (`clock.ts:39`) is the single pinned instant for all seeded rows and is overridable via the `SEED_EPOCH` environment variable. CONSEQUENCE: a `SEED_EPOCH` override moves every seeded row's timestamps while this fixture's rows stay at 2026-04-01, so the two fall out of sync and any rendered document drawing on both would mix epochs. Nothing depends on a `SEED_EPOCH` override today — CI and every capture run use the default — so this is a latent defect, not a live one, and it is filed rather than fixed for that reason. WHAT IS NOT WRONG, recorded so it is not re-investigated: the fixture's own pinning is CORRECT and was a deliberate fix. The comment at `:18-27` records the history — the fixture inserts AFTER `pnpm db:seed` has run its `pin-created-at` pass (F.67), so nothing else pins its rows and `created_at` would otherwise default to `now()`; that reached a rendered document, because `generatedAt` resolves to the source row's `created_at`, and two captures of DSP-REF-0026 differed by exactly one text item, '12:06' against '12:07' (caught Day 27 Phase 1.2). The chosen value follows the same rule `pin-created-at.ts:56-57` uses for seeded rows: the row's own business date at 10:00 UTC = 15:30 IST. So the residual issue is narrow: the value is right but its derivation is duplicated rather than shared. THE GENERAL TRAP REMAINS LIVE for any NEW post-seed `.sql` fixture — anything inserted after `pin-created-at.ts` escapes the pin and must set timestamps explicitly. F.81 avoids it structurally by adding a TypeScript seed module that runs BEFORE `pin-created-at.ts` rather than a post-seed fixture. | F.86  | —     | Convert `day8` seed `computeTotals` from float to Decimal — blast radius measured as zero                                                                       | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-17 during F.81, operator instruction, AFTER the measurement rather than before it. THE DEFECT: `packages/db/src/seeds/day8.ts` `computeTotals` does its money arithmetic on IEEE-754 doubles with `round2 = Math.round(n * 100) / 100`, while `packages/tax` runs every money operation on `decimal.js` — `packages/tax/src/compute.ts` states the rule in its own docstring, "All money math runs on `Decimal` — never native floats". Commit `e32c350` (Q4) aligned the seed's ROUNDING MODEL to production, per-line instead of document-level, but it did not change the SUBSTRATE, and the substrate is the half of the problem that fails silently. MEASURED DIVERGENCE, not deduced: on a 4-line intra-state mixed-rate quotation at rates 18/5/12/5 carrying a 5 percent document discount, the float path yields CGST 9569.34 and the Decimal engine yields CGST 9569.35, a grand total apart by 0.02 rupees. The mechanism is pinned to a single line rather than attributed to "floating point": line taxable 11827.50 at 18 percent splits to a 9 percent CGST half-rate, which is exactly 1064.475 in decimal, but the nearest double is 1064.4749999999999091 — BELOW the tie — so `Math.round` rounds DOWN where `Decimal.ROUND HALF UP` rounds UP. `quotation-engine-parity.test.ts` asserts exact string equality on all seven header money columns, so a document of that shape reaching the corpus turns the parity test red. BLAST RADIUS — MEASURED 2026-09-17 AND ZERO. The conversion was applied on a throwaway branch and the database reseeded from scratch, deliberately while the F.81 harness was warm and both baselines had just been established, because it will never be cheaper to size. Results against the pre-change dump: (1) MONEY — all 260 rows and 1548 numeric fields across `quotations`, `quotation lines`, `performa invoices`, `performa invoice lines`, `orders` and `order lines` byte-identical, of which 938 are header money values across 134 documents. The instrument was every `numeric` column on those six tables, enumerated from `information_schema` rather than listed by hand. The "182 money values" `e32c350` reports was NOT reproduced and no relationship between the two sets is claimed: the obvious candidate subset, quotation headers at seven money columns each, gives 238 here rather than 182. What is established is what the measurement was for — on the enumerated set, which is broader in column coverage than any reading of 182, nothing moved. (2) RENDERS — all 14 Typst cases byte-identical, compared as hashes of RENDERED OUTPUT into a fresh directory, not of `docs/pdf-references/` which is read-only input (DEV.136). (3) `determinism-check` MATCH with `determinism-expected.json` unmodified; `pnpm --filter workers test` 56 of 56; `pnpm --filter @dealerlink/db test` 172 of 172 including `quotation-engine-parity.test.ts`. So the change is a zero-diff no-op on today's corpus and carries no re-baselining cost in any direction. SCOPE: the tax computation inside `computeTotals` only. The other float uses in `day8` — unit-price derivation and `line total` — were left untouched in the measurement and moved nothing; widening to them is a separate judgement, not implied by this row. ORDERING AGAINST F.3, since the question was asked explicitly and the measurement answers it: NOT REQUIRED BEFORE F.3, and the row should not be recorded as an F.3 blocker. `docs/F3_F4_SPEC.md` section 4 invariant 5 asserts exact equality between grouped totals and a direct SUM over the line table, and the hazard would be float-derived stored header totals checked against a Decimal-derived regrouping. But on today's corpus float and Decimal agree EXACTLY — that is precisely what the zero-diff measurement establishes — so that invariant is not threatened by this mechanism and F.3 is not gated on it. NAMING THE REAL TRIGGER, because it is not the one the concern started from: divergence requires a half-paisa tie, a tie requires a mixed-rate document, and in practice it took a discount as well. `day8`'s corpus is single-rate by construction — every seeded product is 18 percent — so no `day8` document can produce one today. F.81's mixed-rate documents are seeded through `computeTax` and are Decimal-derived, so they are consistent by construction too. This row becomes URGENT the moment someone adds a discount-bearing mixed-rate document through `day8`'s `PLANS`, which is a different event from F.3 landing. Recommendation: land it whenever convenient, since it is free, and do not sequence F.3 behind it. SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-09-21 BY OPERATOR RULING, during F.101's prompt approval (its D-4). THIS ROW NOW COVERS A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT, not a new one. F.86 was filed for day8.ts's local computeTotals rounding on IEEE-754 doubles where the production engine uses Decimal. packages/db/src/seeds/day8.ts:258,:268-269 ALSO REIMPLEMENTS THE DOCUMENT-DISCOUNT ALLOCATION on floats — the same proportional per-line allocation that computeTax performs at compute.ts:50,:54 — and it is that reimplementation which wrote the stored headers of every discounted day8 document. THE OPERATOR'S REASONING FOR EXTENDING RATHER THAN FILING A NEIGHBOUR ROW: day8.ts reimplementing the allocation on floats is the same defect as its float computeTotals — seed code duplicating engine logic — and the real fix for both is the same one, day8.ts calling computeTax as packages/db/src/seeds/multi-rate.ts already does. Two rows for one fix would have split the decision. WHY F.101 DOES NOT TOUCH IT: F.101 changes the engine's allocation to largest-remainder, which leaves day8.ts's float reimplementation diverged from the engine in a second way. Mirroring largest-remainder into day8.ts was considered and REJECTED for that day, because changing seed code changes stored seeded data on reseed, which can move rendered reference documents and makes F.101's byte measurement unattributable — the same argument F.55 used when it declined to bundle seed data with a validation change (DEV.139). So F.101 leaves day8.ts alone deliberately and this row inherits the divergence. THE CONDITION THAT MAKES THAT SAFE, AND IT IS MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: F.101 proceeds on its D-4 only if every seeded discounted document has a ZERO allocation residual, so the float and Decimal allocations agree on the existing corpus and no stored header is wrong today. As of 2026-09-21 all 14 discounted seeded QUOTATIONS are measured at 0.00; the eight discounted PIs and the orders are NOT yet measured and F.101's A.0 must cover them. IF ANY RESIDUAL IS NON-ZERO, F.101 STOPS — and this row becomes urgent rather than latent, because a non-zero residual means a stored seeded header disagrees with what the engine would compute. WHEN THIS ROW IS SCHEDULED: fix both instances together by having day8.ts call computeTax, and expect stored seeded numbers to move — which means it needs an operator authorisation covering seeded money columns, a full reference-render measurement set, and deliberate re-baselining of anything that moves. Do not attempt it as a drive-by inside another day. F.81 seeds three rates — 5, 12 and 18 — and deliberately does NOT seed 0 percent. WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ROW AND NOT AN OMISSION: 0 percent is already accepted by every rate list on the render path, so unlike 3 percent it is NOT blocked on F.55. `VALID GST RATES` at `packages/tax/src/compute.ts:7` includes 0, as do the template loaders at `apps/workers/src/templates/quotation.tsx:46` and `performa-invoice.tsx:35`, the Zod schemas in `packages/schemas`, and the two catalogue `select` arrays. A 0 percent product would seed and render today. It was excluded on a different ground: a zero-tax group raises a RENDERING question that F.3 and F.4 have not yet answered — whether a 0 percent group appears in the rate-wise summary as a row with a zero amount, or is suppressed, and the same for its HSN row — and seeding it blind from a seed task would freeze one of those answers before the task that owns the decision has made it. SEQUENCE AFTER F.3/F.4 have decided zero-group rendering. Sibling of F.84 with the same shape and a different blocker: F.84 waits on a type being widened (F.55), this one waits on a rendering decision being taken. UNBLOCKED 2026-09-19 — THE ZERO-RATE RENDERING QUESTION IS SETTLED BY OPERATOR RULING ON F.3 QUESTION Q3. A 0% rate group RENDERS AS A ROW with zero tax amounts, and so does its HSN row. It is NOT suppressed. THE REASON: the group's TAXABLE VALUE is real and non-zero even when its tax is zero, so suppressing the row makes the tax block stop adding up on its own face — the displayed rows would not sum to the displayed taxable total. GSTR-1 also reports nil-rated supply separately, so the row carries real compliance meaning rather than being noise. This ruling is recorded on F.3's row as well, because the two must not drift. TESTABLE BEFORE THIS ROW SHIPS: packages/tax/tests/compute.test.ts already carries a 0%-line fixture, so F.3 can assert the rendering decision without any 0% seed data existing. What F.87 still owes is the FIXTURE — a seeded 0% product and a document carrying it — and per the F.84 precedent it must be appended after the existing seed chains so no prior document counter moves. | F.88  | —     | .claude/worktrees/ is untracked and not gitignored, so `git add -A` would stage a worktree checkout                                                             | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-17, operator instruction, at F.81 closeout. Reported by `verifier` on two consecutive closeout runs as a flag rather than a FAIL, which is the correct classification and also the reason it needs a row: nothing tracked is dirty, so it will keep being reported and keep being waved past. THE FACTS, each checked rather than assumed. `git worktree list` shows two entries — the main checkout at `/workspace`, and a linked worktree at `/workspace/.claude/worktrees/f82-claudemd-gstrate` on branch `worktree-f82-claudemd-gstrate`, left over from the F.82 day and already merged to `main` via PR #38. `git check-ignore -v .claude/worktrees/` exits 1: there is no ignore rule covering it. `/workspace/.gitignore` covers `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.claude/*.local.json` — none of which matches a `worktrees` directory. So a real git checkout sits inside the repository, visible to `git status` as a single untracked directory, and a `git add -A` would attempt to stage its contents. THE SCOPE OF THIS ROW IS THE IGNORE RULE ONLY. Add a pattern covering `.claude/worktrees/` to `/workspace/.gitignore`, and confirm afterwards with `git check-ignore -v` that it matches and that `git status --porcelain` no longer lists the directory. DO NOT REMOVE THE WORKTREE AS PART OF THIS TASK. Operator instruction, stated explicitly at filing time: the registered worktree may be a live working copy belonging to another session, and removing it is the operator's decision, not the implementer's. A `git worktree remove` against a checkout someone is working in destroys uncommitted work with no undo, and the ignore rule solves the reported problem — a stray `git add -A` — without touching it. If the worktree is stale by the time this is picked up, retiring it is a separate decision the operator takes separately. WHY IT IS A ROW AND WAS NOT FOLDED INTO F.81: CLAUDE.md section 11.2 — a process improvement discovered mid-task gets filed, never done. It was noticed during F.81's closeout, it is unrelated to multi-rate seed data, and folding a `.gitignore` edit into a seed commit would put a change nobody reviewed for that purpose into a diff reviewed for something else. | F.89  | —     | PDF loaders throw a bare `Error` with no code on an unexpected GST rate — an unclassified job failure                                                           | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18, operator instruction, from `docs/F55_AUDIT.md` question 2. THIS IS NOT A 3 PERCENT BUG AND SHOULD NOT BE SEQUENCED BEHIND F.55. It is a property of the gap between what the database permits and what the code accepts, and of how the render path fails when it meets a value it did not expect. THE DEFECT. `apps/workers/src/templates/quotation.tsx:49-56` and `apps/workers/src/templates/performa-invoice.tsx:37-41` each define a local `toGstRate()` over a `VALID_GST_RATES` array, and on an unexpected rate each throws a PLAIN `Error` — no error code, no typed class. Both are live on the Typst render path: `apps/workers/src/jobs/render-pdf.ts:33-34` imports the two loaders and calls them at `:84` and `:86`. So the failure surfaces as an UNCLASSIFIED JOB FAILURE rather than a typed, routable validation error, which is the part worth fixing regardless of which rate set the project settles on. Contrast the adjacent path, which degrades better: `convert-quotation-to-pi.ts:86` reaches `computeTax` with no Zod layer in front of it and gets a typed `TaxComputationError` with code `INVALID_GST_RATE`, which `apps/web/lib/actions/pi/helpers.ts:78` maps to `AppError('VALIDATION')`. The engine's guard is coded; the render path's is not. MEASURED 2026-09-17, EXECUTED RATHER THAN TRACED — the audit could only trace it, having no shell. Against the live dev database: inserting a product at `gst_rate` 3 SUCCEEDED and read back as `3.00`; inserting a `quotation_lines` row at 3 onto the real seeded QT-2026-0001 SUCCEEDED; `computeTax` on a 3 percent line threw `TaxComputationError code=INVALID_GST_RATE`; and `loadQuotationPdfData` on QT-2026-0001 then threw `Error code=(none) :: quotation template: unexpected GST rate "3.00"`. THE SHARP FORM OF THAT LAST RESULT: a single out-of-band row made an existing, previously renderable seeded document PERMANENTLY UN-RENDERABLE, with no error code to route on. Probe rows were deleted and the database reseeded clean afterwards; zero products at 3 percent remain. WHY IT IS LATENT AND NOT ACTIVE. No application route can create such a row. All four write gates were tested and all four reject `gstRate: 3` — `createProductSchema`, `updateProductSchema`, `bulkImportProductsSchema` (`packages/schemas/src/product.ts:4`) and `quotationLineInputSchema` (`packages/schemas/src/quotation.ts:42`). The test carried a NON-VACUITY CONTROL: the same probe at 18 percent rejects only on the fixture's missing name and does NOT carry the rate message, so it is the rate refinement firing on 3 and not a generic rejection. The row can therefore only arrive out of band: psql, a seed module, a data import, or a migration. SCOPE AND WHY NARROWING WOULD NOT CLOSE IT. Operator framing, 2026-09-18: narrowing the CHECK constraints back to `(0, 5, 12, 18, 28)` would close THIS INSTANCE and not THE CLASS. The instance is that 3 is currently the one value the database accepts and the code does not. The class is that the render path answers any unexpected data shape with an uncoded `Error`, which stays true whichever rate set is chosen and whichever way F.55 is settled. Sizing this row is about the class. RELATED, NOT BLOCKING: F.55 (which rate set is authoritative), F.84 (3 percent fixture), F.87 (0 percent fixture). This row is independent of all three and can be scheduled without waiting on any of them. | F.90  | —     | R8 is stale — its constraint set is wrong and its worked example moves a product to an abolished slab                                                           | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18, operator instruction, from `docs/GST_RATE_MODEL_AUDIT.md` section 5.2. TWO CONCRETE DEFECTS IN `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` R8 ("Updating product GST rates after a tax change", at `:238`). ONE — `docs/RUNBOOKS.md:244` states as a prerequisite that "The check constraint on `products.gst_rate` only accepts {0, 5, 12, 18, 28}". That is wrong: migration `packages/db/migrations/0017_friendly_logan.sql` widened all four rate constraints to `IN (0, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28)` on 2026-09-07, and the schema files agree (`product.ts:72`, `quotation.ts:171`, `performa-invoice.ts:175`, `order.ts:172`). The same wrong set is repeated at `docs/RUNBOOKS.md:274`, in R8's "Don't" list. TWO — `docs/RUNBOOKS.md:240` gives as its worked example "The GST Council changes the rate on a product category (e.g., HSN 8541 panels move from 18% to 12%)". Per the operator's GST 2.0 report, 12 percent is an abolished slab, so the runbook's illustration walks the reader into moving a product TO a rate that no longer exists. THE SECOND DEFECT DEPENDS ON THE UNVERIFIED SLAB CLAIM and must not be corrected until the operator has confirmed the current slab set with their accountant; the first does not depend on it and is wrong today regardless. SCOPE: correct the two stale statements. Do NOT attempt to fix R8's deeper structural problem in this row — that is recorded on F.55 and is a consequence of whichever validation option is chosen, not a documentation edit. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A DRIVE-BY FIX: CLAUDE.md section 11.2 — a defect found mid-task gets filed, not folded in. It was found during an audit of the rate model, `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` is main-thread-only under section 10.4, and the second correction is blocked on an external confirmation this task cannot obtain. | F.91  | —     | Saving a draft re-stamps its lines with the product master's CURRENT rate, contradicting the stated snapshot contract                                           | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18, operator instruction, from `docs/F55_SPEC.md` section 6. A DEFECT REGARDLESS OF WHICH VALIDATION OPTION WAS CHOSEN, and independent of F.55 — it is about WHERE a line's rate comes from on save, not about which rates are permitted. THE CONTRACT. `packages/schemas/src/quotation.ts:31-32` states it plainly: the line's rate is "captured from product.gst_rate at the moment the line is added — never recomputed at preview/save time". The point of that contract is that a document line is a SNAPSHOT: a quotation issued under one rate keeps that rate even after the product master moves, which is what `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` R8 step 4 also promises — "The change applies to new quotations only. Quotations and invoices already in flight are frozen by design — the tax rate at the time of issue is what's billed." THE CODE DOES NOT HONOUR IT ON UPDATE. `apps/web/lib/actions/quotations/helpers.ts:215-216` re-reads the rate from the product master on save (its own comment says "gst rate + hsn captured from product master at line-creation time") and writes it at `:228`; `apps/web/lib/actions/pi/update-pi.ts:55` does the same with `gstRate: p.gstRate`. So editing an existing draft SILENTLY RE-STAMPS every line with the product's rate as it stands at save time. The snapshot is only as old as the last edit. BLAST RADIUS, stated honestly because it bounds the severity: both update paths are restricted to `draft` status — `update-quotation.ts:19,27-32` and `update-pi.ts:31-33` — so a sent, accepted or confirmed document cannot be re-stamped this way. The exposure is a draft that was created before a rate change and edited after it, which then bills the new rate under its original document date with no record that anything moved. WHY IT MATTERS MORE AFTER F.55, not less: F.55 makes rates freely changeable by the tenant (shape-only validation, no statutory list), so rate changes on the product master become ordinary tenant activity rather than a rare Council-driven event handled by a runbook. The window in which this defect can fire widens accordingly. NOT IN F.55's SCOPE — `docs/F55_SPEC.md` section 6 places it out of scope explicitly, and this row is the "file it" that section calls for. Established in `docs/GST_RATE_MODEL_AUDIT.md` section 3.3, final paragraph. The day prompt that carries this row's origin is `docs/F55_DAY_PROMPT.md`, under "Before the work starts"; the spec section it implements is `docs/F55_SPEC.md` section 6. | F.92  | —     | No as-of / regime concept — a stored rate cannot say which tax regime it was issued under                                                                       | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18, operator instruction, from `docs/F55_SPEC.md` section 6. STANDALONE ROW WITH A POINTER FROM F.6, per the operator: it does not fold into F.84, because F.84 is a fixture task and this is a data-model gap. WHAT EXISTS. The rate is snapshotted BY VALUE onto every document line — `quotation_lines.gst_rate`, `performa_invoice_lines.gst_rate`, `order_lines.gst_rate` — at line-creation time, and copied verbatim by PI-to-Order (`apps/web/lib/actions/pi/status-transitions.ts:189`) and by revision (`apps/web/lib/actions/quotations/revise-quotation.ts:89`). WHAT DOES NOT EXIST. `docs/GST_RATE_MODEL_AUDIT.md` section 3.7 enumerated all 23 modules in `packages/db/src/schema/` and found no rate-version, rate-history, tax-rate or notification module; a grep for `AtIssue\|effective\|valid_from\|version` over that directory returned six hits, ALL of them `tenantStateAtIssue` and its format CHECKs. So THE ONLY "AS OF ISSUE" SNAPSHOT IN THE ENTIRE SCHEMA IS THE TENANT'S STATE, NOT ITS RATE REGIME. `packages/db/src/schema/product.ts` read in full is 22 columns with no effective-from, effective-to or notification-reference beside `gstRate` at `:38`. THE CONSEQUENCE. Preserving the NUMBER is not the same as preserving the CONTEXT. A stored `18.00` cannot say whether it was 18 percent under the pre-22-September-2025 schedule or 18 percent under the current one; the document date is the only temporal anchor and no code joins a rate to it. Option A fixes RENDERING a historical rate — a stored 12 percent document renders, converts and totals once F.55 lands — but it does not make that document IDENTIFIABLE as to the regime it was issued under, and neither would Option B or C. WHY IT BEARS ON F.6. A tax invoice states the rate applied, so the question of which schedule that rate belongs to is a document-content question rather than an internal bookkeeping one. It also bears on credit notes and reprints issued against pre-22-September-2025 documents, where the reprint must reproduce the original rate rather than the current one. NOT SCOPED HERE: whether the answer is a column, a regime table, a notification reference, or nothing at all is a product question nobody has asked yet, and it depends on the transitional treatment the operator is confirming with their accountant. This row records the gap, not the remedy. The day prompt that carries this row's origin is `docs/F55_DAY_PROMPT.md`, under "Before the work starts", where D-1's resolution to option (b) is also what keeps this row standalone rather than folding it into F.84; the spec section it implements is `docs/F55_SPEC.md` section 6. | F.93  | —     | Three `product.test.ts` cases assert only that validation failed, never which field — latently vacuous                                                          | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18 during F.55 closeout, operator instruction to sweep for the shortcut after one instance of it was found. THE ONE THAT WAS ALREADY BROKEN IS FIXED; THESE THREE ARE NOT BROKEN YET, WHICH IS THE POINT. F.55 rewrote `packages/schemas/src/product.test.ts`'s rate case after discovering it had gone VACUOUS rather than inverting: its fixture used `sku: 'X'` and `name: 'X'`, both one character against `min(2)`, so `safeParse` failed on SKU and name and the test stayed GREEN without ever exercising the rate. Measured — the issues were "SKU is required" and "Name is required", and the same fixture with a valid sku/name accepts 10. THE SWEEP FOUND THREE MORE TESTS USING THE SAME SHORTCUT: "rejects HSN code with letters", "rejects HSN code shorter than 4 digits", and "rejects negative MRP". NONE IS CURRENTLY VACUOUS — measured, each one's own subject DOES raise an issue alongside sku and name, so each genuinely exercises its subject today. The defect is structural rather than present: all three assert only `expect(r.success).toBe(false)` and never check WHICH field failed, so all three would keep passing unchanged if HSN validation or the MRP check were deleted tomorrow. They cannot detect the loss of the thing they are named for. THE FIX, which is small: assert on the issue PATH rather than only on failure, and add a control proving that an otherwise-valid fixture raises no issue for that field — the shape F.55 used for the rate cases. OUT OF F.55's SCOPE and filed rather than folded in (CLAUDE.md section 11.2): HSN and MRP validation are untouched by F.55, and widening a day's diff into adjacent tests because one was already being edited is how scope creeps. RELATED: DEV.138 names this as one of four instances of a single signature — a passing negative result is not evidence until something demonstrates it could have failed. | F.94  | —     | `critical-path.spec.ts` flaked once at `moveDealTo`'s post-reload assertion — classify it, do not shrug it                                                      | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-18 during F.55 closeout. REPORTED, NOT CLASSIFIED AND NOT FIXED. `pnpm verify` on F.55's branch reported "1 flaky, 67 passed": `critical-path.spec.ts` failed once and passed on retry number 1. The failing assertion is `moveDealTo`'s post-reload check at `apps/web/tests/e2e/critical-path.spec.ts:125` — `expect(locator('section[data-stage="verbal_commit"] a[href^="/pipeline/"]').filter(...)).toBeVisible()` with a 15 second timeout — reached from `:292`, the `verbal_commit` stage move. WHAT THE DISCRIMINATION SUPPORTS, stated as evidence rather than as a verdict. (1) It is NOT attributable to F.55's change to that file. F.55 changed exactly one line, `:166`, `selectOption` to `fill` on the GST rate input, authorised by D-8. That line is in the product-creation step, which the test must execute successfully BEFORE it can reach `:292`; the test reached `:292`, so the changed line worked. (2) It got FURTHER on retry rather than failing identically, which is the discrimination DEV.93 established between a timing flake and a state bug. WHAT HAS NOT BEEN DONE: the classification has not been established by repetition, which is the only thing that would settle it. `flake-triager` exists for exactly this and was not run, because the invocation costs several full-suite runs and the operator should choose whether that is worth it now. NOTHING WAS WEAKENED TO GET GREEN: no timeout was raised, no spec was skipped or `fixme`-d, and no spec was retried harder (CLAUDE.md section 11.1 ruling 1). The retry that passed is Playwright's own configured retry, not an intervention. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE: Day 24's flake-reclassification commit put the standard plainly — a flake should register "as new signal rather than a known-flake shrug" — and there is no existing record of this spec flaking at `moveDealTo`, checked against DEVIATIONS.md. DECIDED 2026-09-18, OPERATOR RULING: DO NOT SPEND `flake-triager`'s RUNS ON THIS. THIS ROW IS A DECISION, NOT A GAP. The cause is already diagnosed and already filed: **F.68** — "critical-path e2e: an 800ms sleep races the stage-transition commit, and that is the flake's actual cause" — names `moveDealTo`, the 800ms sleep, `transitionDealStage`'s commit, and the reloaded `force-dynamic` page rendering the stale column. Verified against F.68's own notes before recording this, rather than cited from memory. The observed failure matches that diagnosis exactly: the assertion that failed is `moveDealTo`'s POST-RELOAD check, the one that re-reads the board from the database after a stage move, and it passed on retry. WHY CLASSIFICATION WOULD ADD NOTHING: `flake-triager` establishes whether a failure is a TIMING FLAKE or a STATE BUG by repetition. Here the mechanism is already known and already has a row with a fix attached, so a classification run would confirm what is known rather than resolve anything open — and it costs several full-suite runs at roughly fifteen minutes each. THIS IS THE SAME REASONING THAT PUT `verify-day-c1` LAST IN F.52's TRIAGE ORDER: effort goes to failures whose cause is genuinely unknown, not to ones where repetition would only re-observe a documented mechanism. Recording the reason matters because an unexplained "not triaged" reads as an omission in six months, and the next person spends the runs anyway. WHAT REOPENS THIS: a recurrence on CI whose signature DIFFERS from F.68's — a different assertion, a different helper, a failure that does NOT get further on retry (which is DEV.93's discrimination for a state bug), or a failure in a stage move that does not involve the post-reload read. Any of those is new signal and is not covered by this decision. A recurrence matching F.68's signature is not, and should be folded into F.68 rather than re-filed here. NOTE ON THE SUPERSEDING RELATIONSHIP: F.68 owns the FIX (removing the sleep in favour of waiting on the transition's effect); this row owns only the observation that it recurred during F.55 and the decision not to re-diagnose it. If F.68 lands, this row closes with it. SECOND OBSERVED SIGNATURE, 2026-09-20, during F.3's pnpm verify (73 passed, 1 flaky). DIFFERENT SITE, SAME FAMILY: critical-path.spec.ts:300, step "13. convert quotation to a PI", locator getByRole('heading', { name: /New PI from/ }), toBeVisible timeout, recovered on retry #1. The first signature was step "8. advance deal to needs_analysis" at moveDealTo (:125), locator section[data-stage="needs_analysis"] a[href^="/pipeline/"]. OPERATOR RULING: both are navigation-or-render timeouts on a page just committed to, recovering on retry — the F.52 signature — so this is the same cause at a second location and does NOT reopen the task. flake-triager was NOT run. THE REOPENING CONDITION IS TIGHTENED BECAUSE THE OLD ONE MISFIRED. It previously read that a signature differing from F.68's reopens this row; that condition fired here on a difference of LOCATION when it was written to catch a difference of CAUSE. It is replaced by three conditions, any one of which reopens: a RED CI RUN (not a local flake that passes on retry); TWO OBSERVATIONS AT THE SAME SITE (one observation anywhere is noise, two at one locator is a pattern); or A FAILURE THAT DOES NOT RECOVER ON RETRY (which is DEV.93's discrimination — a state bug fails identically every run and gets no further on retry, a timing flake does not). F.3 IS NOT THE CAUSE, AND THIS IS THE EVIDENCE SOMEBODY WILL WANT LATER: the heading is rendered by apps/web/app/(app)/quotations/[id]/convert-to-pi/page.tsx, which F.3 did not modify — git status over apps/web lists eleven modified files and that is not among them. Its five imports were checked individually and none changed: getAuthContext from lib/auth/session, listDealers from lib/queries/dealers, getQuotationById from lib/queries/quotations, impersonationTenantId from lib/tenant/context, and its own local ConvertToPiForm. The one component F.3 did change on that route tree, SummaryCard, is imported by exactly one file, quotation-builder-form.tsx:21, and used at :292 — not by the convert page. So there is no path, direct or indirect, from F.3's diff to the failing locator. | F.96  | —     | `listTenantGstRates` filters neither `deleted_at` nor `status`, so rate suggestions include inactive and discontinued products                                  | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-19, operator instruction, found while drafting F.84. THIS IS A DEFECT IN CODE SHIPPED ON 2026-09-18, NOT A TEST PROBLEM. `apps/web/lib/queries/products.ts` — `listTenantGstRates` selects distinct `gst_rate` with a WHERE clause of `eq(products.tenantId, tenantId)` AND NOTHING ELSE. It filters neither `deleted_at IS NULL` nor `status = 'active'`. WHAT THAT MEANS ON A USER-VISIBLE SURFACE: the function feeds the GST-rate SUGGESTION datalist on both catalogue screens — `/catalog/new` and the product-detail pricing editor — and it also feeds the new-product form's placeholder via `String(knownGstRates[0])`. So a tenant that marked a product 'inactive' or 'discontinued' still sees that product's rate offered as a suggestion, with no indication of where it came from. It also drives the D-6 'unusual rate' warning: a rate is treated as FAMILIAR if any row carries it, including a deleted one, so the warning silently stops firing for a rate the tenant has deliberately retired. THE SYMPTOM THAT SURFACED IT, which is NOT the finding: `apps/web/tests/e2e/verify-day-f55.spec.ts` saves a product at 40 percent and asserts the D-6 warning appears first. On a second LOCAL run without an intervening reseed, 40 is already a known rate, `rateIsUnusual` is false, the first click saves, and the assertion fails. CI is immune because the e2e job reseeds; local reruns are not. Same family as DEV.91. Recording that distinction deliberately: fixing only the test would leave the real defect in place and remove the thing that made it visible. WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS, not scoped here: filter `status`, and add `deleted_at IS NULL` at the same time as forward-safety. `searchProducts` in the same module is the nearest precedent — it filters `eq(products.status, 'active')` — but it does NOT filter `deleted_at`, and neither does `listProducts`, so the precedent covers only half the fix. Whether `active` is the right set is a judgement rather than a reflex: an 'inactive' product's rate is arguably still one the tenant uses, while a 'discontinued' one probably is not. AND ONE HALF OF THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS NOT REACHABLE, CORRECTED BEFORE THE ROW WAS COMMITTED. It said suggestions include rates from DELETED products. Measured: `packages/db/src/schema/product.ts:64` declares `deletedAt`, but a grep for `deletedAt` across `apps/web/lib/actions/products/` returns nothing — there is NO soft-delete path for products anywhere in the application, so no product row carries a `deleted_at` today and no suggestion can come from one. The live half is `status`, and it stands. The `deleted_at` finding survives as something different and more durable: `products.deleted_at` is a COLUMN WITH NO WRITER, and `CLAUDE.md` section 4 says soft delete applies to Product and that queries filter it via a Drizzle helper — yet no query in `apps/web/lib/queries/products.ts` filters it, not this one, not `listProducts`, not `searchProducts`. The only query module under `apps/web/lib/queries/` that filters `deletedAt` at all is `payments.ts`. So when product soft-delete is implemented, three queries in that module become wrong together and this is the least visible of them. Adding the filter now is cheap; claiming it fixes a present-day leak was not accurate, and the claim was made within a day of DEV.138, which is about exactly that kind of unearned precision. NOT FIXED IN F.84 (CLAUDE.md section 11.2): F.84 is a fixture-and-coverage day, this is an `apps/web` query defect, and F.84's own fixture adds a 3 percent product that changes the suggestion set — folding a behavioural fix into that diff would make both harder to review. WORTH NOTING FOR SEQUENCING: F.84's e2e spec must not assert a D-6 warning at 3 percent, because the fixture makes 3 familiar. That is already recorded in F.84's day prompt. Measured on a freshly seeded dev DB 2026-09-19: `SELECT count(*) FROM performa_invoices` returns 64, and the count of those with no matching performa_invoice_lines row returns 38. Enumerating which seeds write which table: packages/db/src/seeds/day11.ts, day12.ts, day13.ts and multi-rate.ts all insert PI headers, but only day11.ts and multi-rate.ts insert PI lines. So day12.ts and day13.ts create PI headers with stored money totals and no line detail behind them. PRE-EXISTING AND NOT CAUSED BY F.81 OR F.84: both of those add PIs with lines (F.84 adds exactly two, PI-2026-0032 for each tenant, both with two 3% lines). WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: a PI header carries subtotal, taxable, CGST/SGST/IGST and total as stored money columns, so a zero-line PI is a document whose totals cannot be re-derived from its own lines. That is exactly the shape quotation-engine-parity.test.ts:51-101 checks for quotations and nothing checks for PIs, and any future PI-side parity test, PI PDF render, or GST summary report that reads PI lines will see 38 documents that look empty while their headers claim money. It also means a PI render test cannot pick a seeded PI at random. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: decide whether day12/day13 PIs should get lines, or whether those headers should not exist; this touches seeded money columns, so it needs the same operator authorisation shape F.81 and F.84 used. | F.98  | —     | DEVIATIONS.md is not in .prettierignore, so the pre-commit hook can rewrite historic entries                                                                    | ⏳     | —          | Found during F.84's closeout and FILED RATHER THAN FIXED per CLAUDE.md section 11.2; the verifier FAIL it caused was accepted by the operator on F.84's branch (Option A) with the reformat kept. THE GAP: package.json lint-staged runs `prettier --write` on `*.{json,css,md,yaml,yml}`, and .prettierignore (10 entries, read in full: .next, node*modules, dist, build, coverage, *.min.js, pnpm-lock.yaml, .pnpm-store/, test-results/, playwright-report/) does not list DEVIATIONS.md. So staging that file hands the whole thing to prettier, which rewrites every line it disagrees with — including entries written months earlier. On F.84's branch, at commit 7161d1a, this modified 14 lines inside the DEV.138 and DEV.139 entries, breaching the append-only rule the file exists to uphold. Reproduce the exact set with `git diff -U0 edf8d3f..7161d1a -- DEVIATIONS.md` rather than by line number: the DEV.138 table gained a sixth row later the same day, so every line number below it has shifted and any figure quoted here would already be wrong. The content was provably unchanged — `*em\*`to`\_em*`and table-cell padding only, checked hunk by hunk — so nothing in the record was falsified. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: add DEVIATIONS.md to .prettierignore. Consider DECISIONS.md and docs/PROJECT_HISTORY.md on the same argument — any append-only or hand-maintained record of past decisions has the same exposure. PROJECT_PLAN.md is generated so prettier cannot corrupt a decision there, but note that plan:sync's output must itself stay prettier-clean or the hook and the generator will fight; check that before adding or omitting it. WHY THIS IS NOW A ONE-TIME DEBT AND NOT A RECURRING TRAP, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: before F.84, DEVIATIONS.md was not a prettier fixed point, so the first commit to stage it normalised nine hunks of accumulated drift. After F.84 it IS a fixed point —`prettier --write DEVIATIONS.md`leaves the file byte-identical, and an in-repo append simulation (a copy inside the working tree, so .prettierrc resolves) leaves all 6,136 historic lines untouched while rewriting only the appended text. Confirmed live on the DEV.138 edit that followed: all six hunks fell inside DEV.138's own region. So the remaining exposure is narrow — a prettier version bump or a .prettierrc change would make the file unclean again and the next commit would re-normalise history wholesale. That is the case the .prettierignore entry prevents. SECOND, INDEPENDENT FINDING — THE HOOK CAN APPARENTLY NOT RUN, AND THIS IS UNEXPLAINED. Commits ead233e (+193 -0) and c4b8a77 (+282 -0) both staged DEVIATIONS.md, and both left it with ZERO deletions while the file was still not prettier-clean at those revisions (re-checked with`--config /workspace/.prettierrc`after an earlier check on /tmp copies proved invalid). If`prettier --write`had run, the file would have been rewritten and would have been clean afterwards. It was not. So on those two commits the hook either did not run, did not include this file, or failed silently. NOTHING IN GIT DISTINGUISHES THAT FROM`--no-verify`: there is no recorded signal for whether a hook executed. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PRETTIER: if the pre-commit hook can silently not run, then every guarantee that rests on it is conditional rather than enforced — the same class as CLAUDE.md section 10.5's honest admission about Bash permission prefixes. The append-only rule has a hole here that is independent of prettier and would survive fixing .prettierignore. Worth investigating whether lint-staged failures are surfaced at all, and whether CI can assert what the hook is supposed to guarantee (a `git diff`scope check on DEVIATIONS.md against the merge base would catch a historic-line edit regardless of how it got there, which is the enforcement CLAUDE.md section 10.3 says does not currently exist). THIRD FINDING, RECORDED AS DEV.138 MEMBER 6 RATHER THAN HERE, AND NAMED SO THIS ROW CARRIES ALL THREE: the first cleanliness evidence for everything above was INVALID.`prettier --check` was run on /tmp copies of DEVIATIONS.md, and .prettierrc resolves from the file own path upward, so every one of those runs used DEFAULT config — a different singleQuote and printWidth than this repo sets. Three claims rested on it: that origin/main was unclean, that four named revisions were unclean, and that a future append would rewrite history. Re-run with --config inside the repo the conclusion held and no reported fact was wrong, but the evidence did not exist until then. It is the first member of the DEV.138 family caught before shipping, and it was caught by an output that did not fit rather than by review: the simulation reported historic lines changing in a way the stated mechanism (emphasis markers, table padding) could not produce, having rewritten single quotes to double inside a fenced code block, which is a config difference and not a content one. THE TRANSFERABLE PART, which is why it belongs near this row: lint, format, typecheck and test configuration is all path-resolved, so copying a file out of the tree to inspect it silently strips the config that governs it. Any work on this row will be tempted to do exactly that again. DO NOT FOLD EITHER HALF INTO AN UNRELATED DAY. FOURTH FINDING, DISCOVERED BY THIS ROW BREAKING CI ON ITS OWN PR (#49, checks red in 25s): A NOTES FIELD IN docs/stage-f-tasks.json MUST NOT CONTAIN A BLANK-LINE PARAGRAPH BREAK. scripts/sync-project-plan.ts sanitize() at :229 maps every control character, newline included, to a SINGLE SPACE, so an \\n\\n becomes a DOUBLE space inside the rendered markdown table cell. Prettier collapses consecutive spaces in a table cell, the pre-commit hook therefore rewrites the generated file, and plan:check then fails against plan:sync output — the generator and the hook fighting over the same line, which is the exact failure mode this row predicted in its SCOPE paragraph one commit before causing it. Measured: F.98 rendered 4 double-spaces inside its notes prose against 0 for F.96 and F.97, whose notes are a single paragraph. This row notes are now a single paragraph for that reason. THE GENERAL FIX BELONGS WITH THIS ROW because it is the same prettier-versus-generated-file conflict: either add PROJECT_PLAN.md to .prettierignore, or have sanitize() collapse runs of whitespace so its output is a prettier fixed point by construction. The second is better — it makes the invariant hold rather than exempting the file from the checker — but it is a change to a script with its own test suite and it is NOT in scope for a row that currently changes no code. | F.99  | —     | No per-line tax is stored at any grain, so every consumer recomputes and a historical document is reproducible only as-if-billed-today                          | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-19 during F.3's pre-day scoping, from the operator's ruling on F.3 question Q2. THE MEASUREMENT: all three line tables were enumerated in full from information_schema on 2026-09-19 — quotation_lines, performa_invoice_lines and order_lines each store hsn_code, quantity, unit_price, gst_rate and line_total, and NO per-line tax, taxable-value or discount column at any grain. Tax is persisted only on the document header: subtotal, discount_amount, taxable_amount, cgst_amount, sgst_amount, igst_amount, total_amount. THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS LARGER THAN ANY ONE ROW: because no per-line or per-group tax is stored, EVERY consumer must recompute it through computeTax — the GST Summary report's future rate axis, F.11's Tally export, F.6's tax invoice, and F.3/F.4's HSN table. That is safe only for as long as the engine's rounding model never changes. THE FAILURE MODE: the moment it changes, a historical document recomputes differently from the way it was actually billed, and nothing records which engine produced the original figures. The document's stored header totals would then disagree with its own recomputed breakdown, and there is no way to tell which is right. SAME SHAPE AS F.92, AND THEY SHOULD BE READ TOGETHER: F.92 is that a stored rate cannot say which tax REGIME it was issued under; this row is that a stored total cannot say which ENGINE VERSION produced it. Both reduce to the same principle — a historical document should be reproducible AS BILLED, not as-if-billed-today. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED BY F.3: F.3 composes on top of computeTax and reconciles its grouped output against the stored headers exactly, which is correct today and is what the operator authorised; this row is about the durability of that arrangement, not its correctness. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: decide between persisting the per-line tax breakdown at write time, stamping documents with an engine version, or accepting recomputation and pinning the rounding model with a test that fails if it changes. This touches money columns on four tables, so it needs the same operator authorisation shape F.55, F.81 and F.84 used. Cross-reference F.92. | F.100 | —     | CLAUDE.md section-anchor citations are unguarded — two wrong ones found, and neither check:ids nor check:paths can see them                                     | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-19 during F.3's pre-day scoping. TWO CONFIRMED INSTANCES, both citing a CLAUDE.md section that does not say what the citing text claims. FIRST: apps/web/lib/reports/gst-summary.ts:8 cites "CLAUDE.md section 6" for the rule that every figure is the order's STORED tax amount. Section 6 is Auth and Roles; the stored-money rule is at CLAUDE.md:465, inside section 10. SECOND: docs/F3_F4_SPEC.md section 3 cited "CLAUDE.md section 19" for the same rule. CLAUDE.md has sections 0 through 11 only, so section 19 has never existed. That one was corrected in place on 2026-09-19 as part of F.3's spec amendment; the gst-summary.ts one is NOT yet fixed and is this row's concrete work. THE GAP THIS ROW IS ACTUALLY ABOUT: nothing can catch either. pnpm check:ids validates cited DEV and ADR ids resolve to entries; pnpm check:paths validates cited file paths exist. A SECTION ANCHOR is neither, so a citation to a nonexistent or wrong section passes every gate and reads exactly as authoritative as a correct one. SAME CLASS AS DEV.128's finding that a wrong id is not self-correcting because every downstream citation looks exactly as authoritative as a right one — and the same reason check:ids was written in the first place. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO: a reader following gst-summary.ts:8 to CLAUDE.md section 6 finds role permissions, concludes the comment is wrong or the rule was moved, and may weaken a compliance-critical constraint on that basis. The comment's actual claim is correct; only its address is wrong. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: fix gst-summary.ts:8, then decide whether a checker is worth it. A checker would need to parse CLAUDE.md's heading structure and validate every "CLAUDE.md section N" or "CLAUDE.md §N" reference across the repo; consider also whether section NUMBERS should be replaced by stable slugs, since renumbering CLAUDE.md would silently invalidate every existing citation at once. Enumerate the full population before deciding — git grep -nE 'CLAUDE\\.md[^0-9]{0,15}(§\|section )[0-9]+' — rather than fixing the two known instances and assuming they are all. | F.102 | —     | DEV.138's instance table is a bounded append-only exception — the rule now says so, because three accepts had not                                               | ✅     | 2026-09-20 | Done 2026-09-20 on this branch (F.3's closeout), as Option C of an operator ruling on a verifier FAIL. THE FAIL WAS CORRECT AND WAS NOT OVERRULED: DEV.138 was edited in place — heading six to seven, the scope line, the "The six" sentence, the "covers all six" sentence, plus a new instance-table row and prettier's mechanical re-padding of the existing rows. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: the same amendment had been correctly flagged by verifier and operator-accepted THREE times — the fifth instance in commit 0661c97, the sixth earlier in the same session on PR #48, and the seventh here — and each accept changed nothing. Three accepts of one breach means the convention lives only in decisions nobody reading the repository can find, and AN EXPECTED FAIL IS ONE THAT STOPS BEING READ. That is the cost, not the fourteen modified lines. Accepting a fourth time without changing the rule would have bought nothing. WHAT CHANGED, IN THE SAME PR RATHER THAN LATER, because a row on its own would have left the FAIL recurring: .claude/agents/verifier.md section 3 and docs/BUILD_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md (both the C6 step and the Deviations log section) now state ONE BOUNDED EXCEPTION. DEV.138 is a LIVING INDEX of one recurring signature, and the following may be edited in place — rows of its instance table, including a new row and prettier's re-padding of existing rows when one is added; and the four derived counts that must agree with the table, namely the heading's instance count, the scope line naming which entries carry the instances, the "The N" sentence, and the "covers all N" sentence. THE BOUND IS EXHAUSTIVE, NOT ILLUSTRATIVE, and that is the operator's reasoning verbatim: an exception to append-only that is not bounded becomes a general permission. Everything else in DEV.138 — its findings, its rule statement, its discussion paragraphs, its closing section — stays append-only exactly like every other entry, and NO OTHER ENTRY HAS ANY EXCEPTION AT ALL. A modified line inside DEV.138 that is not a table row or one of those four counts is still a FAIL. verifier is now required to NAME the lines it classified as covered when it takes the exception, so the boundary is applied visibly rather than assumed. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, and the reasoning is the part worth keeping: leaving DEV.138 at six instances and carrying later ones in each day's own entry would satisfy the rule exactly. It was rejected because DEV.138's own closing paragraph turns on the enumeration being in one place — "the next instance will not look like any of the N, so recognising it requires the signature rather than the examples". The verifier argued the amendment was redundant because the day's entry already cites DEV.138; both citations were checked and both invoke DEV.138's RULE, while NEITHER registers a seventh INSTANCE, so a reader arriving at DEV.138 would still count six. Compliance would have been bought by giving up the property the entry exists for. WHAT A FUTURE READER SHOULD DO: if the bound ever needs widening, widen it here and in both rule sites in the same change, and state which property of the entry the widening protects. If DEV.138 stops being the index — if the signature gets its own document, for instance — DELETE this exception rather than leaving it as a standing permission attached to nothing. Recorded in DEV.143. | F.104 | —     | The accessibility scan covers four pages; the quotation view, PI view and a non-empty builder are unscanned and share the pattern that just failed              | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-22 during F.3's a11y fix, as a coverage gap that stands on its own rather than as part of that defect. WHAT IS SCANNED TODAY: apps/web/tests/e2e/verify-day-16.spec.ts runs axe on four pages only — the dashboard, the dealers list and detail, /quotations/new, and order detail. WHAT IS NOT: /quotations/[id], /pi/[id], and a quotation builder WITH LINES. THE GAP MATTERS BECAUSE OF WHAT THOSE THREE SHARE. All four call sites of TaxSummaryBlock render it directly inside a dl element — apps/web/app/(app)/orders/[id]/page.tsx, pi/[id]/page.tsx, quotations/[id]/page.tsx and quotations/\_components/summary-card.tsx — and the defect fixed on this branch was precisely a DOM-structure violation of that dl. Only ONE of those four call sites is scanned. NOTE WHAT /quotations/new DOES AND DOES NOT COVER: it IS scanned, but an EMPTY builder renders the component's empty branch, which emits a single dt/dd pair and no rate rows at all, so it exercises none of the structure that failed. A builder with lines is a different page for this purpose and is not scanned by anything. THE CLAIM THAT THOSE THREE ALSO CARRIED THE DEFECT IS INFERENCE, NOT MEASUREMENT, and must stay recorded as such: it rests on reading the four call sites and confirming each places the component directly inside a dl, plus the component being shared, plus the violation being a property of the component's own markup rather than of any page. NO SPEC SCANNED THEM BEFORE OR AFTER THE FIX, so nothing was observed either way. A future reader must not cite this row as evidence that those pages were broken. THE FIX ON THIS BRANCH COVERS THEM BY CONSTRUCTION, because they share the component and the change is to the component, so this row is NOT about repairing anything — it is about the scan being narrower than the pattern it is meant to protect. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE: extending the scan is not evidence for the fix and was not needed to verify it, so folding it in would have widened an accessibility fix into a coverage project mid-branch, against CLAUDE.md section 11.2. SCOPE WHEN SCHEDULED: add axe scans for /quotations/[id], /pi/[id] and a builder carrying at least one line. Resolve the documents by SHAPE rather than by number, and require an intra-state document with a taxable line for at least one of them, for the reason recorded in DEV.144 — the intra-state branch is the one that renders a CGST/SGST pair per rate, the inter-state branch returns a single row directly and was never structurally at risk, so a scan that lands on an inter-state document passes whether or not the markup is correct. Each new scan needs the same non-vacuity guard the pinned order scan now carries: assert the tax rows are actually on the page before asserting that axe found nothing, or a page that failed to render the block would scan clean and pass for the wrong reason. | F.107 | —     | CLAUDE.md section 10.3 names three required status checks; the ruleset requires four — typst-determinism is enforced and undocumented                           | ⏳     | —          | Filed 2026-09-24 by operator ruling, found while checking a verifier observation on PR #57 and NOT fixed there — CLAUDE.md section 11.2 says a process improvement discovered mid-task gets filed, never folded into the branch that found it. THE DRIFT: CLAUDE.md section 10.3 line 526 reads "the three required status checks (checks, test, e2e)", and section 10.5 line 560 says "The real enforcement is branch protection and the required status checks on main". The repository ruleset named "PR Main" (id 22424469, target branch, enforcement active) requires FOUR contexts, enumerated from the API rather than inferred: e2e, test, checks, AND typst-determinism. So typst-determinism gates every merge to main and no document says so. This matters because section 10.3 is the passage whose whole purpose is telling a reader which gates are actually enforced as against which are convention, so an undercount there is the one kind of error that section cannot afford. Confirmed on PR #57, where all four reported and the PR stayed BLOCKED until the fourth finished. SECOND, SEPARATE POINT — THE 404 IS A TRAP AND THE NOTE SHOULD SAY SO. main is NOT protected by classic branch protection, so GET /repos/dealerlink/dealerlink/branches/main/protection returns HTTP 404 with the message "Branch not protected". That reads as "main is unprotected" to anyone who checks it that way, and it is wrong: protection is implemented as a RULESET, which that endpoint does not report. The rules on main are deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request and required_status_checks, readable at GET /repos/dealerlink/dealerlink/rules/branches/main or GET /repos/dealerlink/dealerlink/rulesets. Whoever fixes this row should add the instrument alongside the claim, because the failure mode here is not a wrong fact but a right fact checked with the wrong tool returning a confident wrong answer — the same shape as ruling 8 about plain grep. SCOPE: a wording correction to CLAUDE.md sections 10.3 and 10.5 naming four checks and the ruleset mechanism, plus a check of whether any other document repeats the count of three. No code, no workflow change, no ruleset change — the ruleset is correct as it stands and this row is about the documentation describing it. Cross-references DEV.145 only insofar as both came out of the F.105/F.103 sequence.
